21	**[Section 1: Executive Summary]{.underline}**
22	
23	Stratton Forensic Consulting LLC (\"Stratton\") was engaged by Halstead, Rowe & Kimball LLP (\"HRK\") on January 22, 2025, to perform forensic imaging, collection, and processing of electronically stored information (\"ESI\") and hard-copy documents from four designated custodians identified in the Grand Jury Subpoena Duces Tecum issued on January 14, 2025, in connection with Grand Jury No. 24-GJ-0387. The subpoena carried an original return date of February 28, 2025, which was subsequently extended through negotiation with the U.S. Attorney\'s Office to April 15, 2025 for the first rolling production and June 30, 2025 for final production of all responsive, non-privileged materials.
24	
25	The four custodians designated for collection are as follows:
26	
27	1.**Garrett Whitford**, Managing Partner, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC
28	
29	2.**Diana Cheng-Rourke**, Partner, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC
30	
31	3.**Tobias Krell**, Vice President, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC
32	
33	4.**Dr. Priya Anand**, former Chief Executive Officer, MedCore Diagnostics Inc. (2020--2022)
34	
35	The relevant time period specified in the subpoena spans from January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023. Collections were performed between January 27, 2025 and March 15, 2025, encompassing corporate email accounts, corporate-issued laptops and workstations, personal mobile devices, and certain non-custodial corporate repositories. All collected data was processed in Relativity, hosted on Stratton\'s secure cloud environment, and made available to HRK\'s document review team beginning February 10, 2025 on a rolling basis as processing was completed.
36	
37	The aggregate collection results are as follows: a total of **52,318 unique documents** were ingested into Relativity across all custodians and non-custodial sources after cross-custodian and cross-source de-duplication.
38	
39	This memorandum documents the methodology, data sources, volumes, and any issues or exceptions encountered during the collection process. Several significant collection gaps and exceptions are noted herein and require counsel\'s immediate attention. These include the following critical items:
40	
41	\(a\) **Incomplete collection from Garrett Whitford\'s personal mobile device** --- Mr. Whitford\'s personal iPhone was factory reset on or about January 20, 2025, approximately six days after the subpoena was issued, resulting in the total loss of Signal and WhatsApp data and only partial recovery of iMessage data from an iCloud backup predating the reset;
42	
43	\(b\) **Uncollected personal Gmail account and personal iPhone for Dr. Priya Anand** --- Dr. Anand acknowledged using a personal Gmail account for certain business-related communications, and her personal mobile device has not been collected, both pending negotiation with Dr. Anand\'s independent counsel, which has not responded to Stratton\'s proposed collection protocol transmitted on March 5, 2025; and
44	
45	\(c\) **Uncollected MedCore Board --- Corporate Secretary SharePoint site** --- A SharePoint site maintained by MedCore\'s corporate secretary, containing board of directors meeting minutes and board packages for all quarters during the Ridgeline ownership period, has not been collected due to pending access coordination with Veriton Health Systems, the current owner of MedCore\'s IT infrastructure.
46	
47	Each of these items is discussed in detail in the custodian-specific and source-specific sections below and is consolidated with Stratton\'s recommendations in Section 7 of this memorandum.
48	
49	**[Section 2: Engagement Background and Scope]{.underline}**
50	
51	Stratton was engaged under the direction of HRK, specifically lead partner Margaret Halstead and senior associate Jordan Tavares, in connection with the defense and representation of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC (\"Ridgeline\" or \"RCP\"), a Delaware limited liability company formed in 2014 and headquartered at 595 Madison Avenue, 22nd Floor, New York, NY 10022. Ridgeline is a mid-market private equity fund with approximately \$2.8 billion in assets under management across three active fund vehicles: Ridgeline Capital Fund II LP, Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP, and Ridgeline Capital Fund IV LP.
52	
53	The investigation by the U.S. Attorney\'s Office for the Southern District of New York, conducted by AUSA Bradley Navarro, concerns the acquisition of MedCore Diagnostics Inc. (\"MedCore\"), a Delaware corporation with principal offices formerly located at 2100 Lakewood Boulevard, Suite 400, Durham, NC 27703, by Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP in March 2020 for approximately \$185 million, and the subsequent sale of MedCore to Veriton Health Systems Inc. (\"Veriton\") in November 2022 for approximately \$410 million. The nature and specific theories of the government\'s investigation have not been disclosed to Stratton and are beyond the scope of this memorandum; however, Stratton understands from HRK that the subpoena\'s eighteen numbered request categories encompass communications, financial records, regulatory filings, due diligence materials, board minutes, valuation analyses, and other documents relating to Ridgeline\'s acquisition, ownership, management, and sale of MedCore during the period January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023.
54	
55	The Grand Jury Subpoena Duces Tecum (Grand Jury No. 24-GJ-0387) was issued on January 14, 2025 and contains eighteen numbered request categories spanning the identified time period. The scope of Stratton\'s engagement encompasses the following activities: forensic imaging of custodian laptops and workstations; collection of corporate email accounts (Microsoft Exchange / Outlook 365); extraction of mobile device data (including iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, and SMS/MMS); collection of network file shares and cloud-based repositories as directed by counsel; and processing and ingestion of all collected data into the Relativity review platform for use by HRK\'s document review team.
56	
57	Non-custodial sources, including corporate repositories, shared drives, and document management systems, were identified during the initial scoping phase but collection of most non-custodial sources was deferred to a second phase, except as specifically noted in Section 5 of this memorandum. The decision to prioritize custodian-level collections in the first phase was made by HRK in consultation with Stratton, given the production timeline and the need to begin document review as quickly as possible.
58	
59	HRK\'s engagement letter with Stratton is dated January 22, 2025, and Stratton commenced collection activities on January 27, 2025.
60	
61	**[Section 3: Collection Methodology --- General]{.underline}**
62	
63	The following describes the general methodologies employed by Stratton during the collection engagement. Custodian-specific deviations, exceptions, and additional details are noted in Section 4 below.
64	
65	**Forensic Imaging of Computers.** All laptop and desktop devices identified for collection were forensically imaged using Tableau T35689iu write-blocking hardware to prevent any alteration of the source media. Forensic images were created using FTK Imager (version 4.7) in EnCase Evidence File (.E01) format. SHA-256 hash values were calculated for each forensic image at the time of creation and were verified against the source media to confirm bit-for-bit integrity. Chain of custody forms were executed for each device at the time of intake and again upon return of the device to the custodian or to Ridgeline\'s IT department. All forensic images are maintained on Stratton\'s secure evidence servers with restricted access controls and are available for verification upon request.
66	
67	**Email Collection.** Corporate email hosted on Microsoft Exchange Online (Microsoft 365) was collected via remote journal extraction from Ridgeline\'s Microsoft 365 tenant, with administrative access provided by Ridgeline\'s IT Director, Mark Ellison. For Dr. Anand, corporate email was collected from MedCore\'s separate Exchange environment, which is now maintained by Veriton Health Systems\' IT department. Collections targeted each custodian\'s primary mailbox, sent items folder, deleted items folder (including recoverable deleted items within the Exchange retention window), and online archive mailbox where applicable. A date range filter of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023 was applied at the point of extraction to limit the volume of data collected to the subpoena\'s relevant time period. All email data was extracted in PST format for processing.
68	
69	**Mobile Device Collection.** Where personal mobile devices were made available by custodians, Stratton utilized Cellebrite UFED (version 7.68) and, where necessary, GrayKey (version 2024.3) extraction tools to perform physical or logical extractions, depending on the device model, operating system version, and available extraction capabilities. The scope of mobile device extraction included iMessage conversations (via device extraction or iCloud backup, as applicable), WhatsApp local application database files, Signal local application database files (where the application was installed), and SMS/MMS messages. Extraction reports were generated in Cellebrite\'s native format and subsequently processed for ingestion into Relativity.
70	
71	**Cloud Account Collection.** For personal cloud email accounts (e.g., Gmail), Stratton\'s collection protocol calls for extraction via Google Takeout or API-based extraction tools, with the custodian\'s written authorization and, where the custodian is represented by independent counsel, with the consent of that counsel. The specific status of personal cloud account collections is discussed in the custodian-specific sections below.
72	
73	**Processing.** All collected data was processed in Relativity (version 2024.2), hosted on Stratton\'s secure cloud environment (Microsoft Azure, East US region, SOC 2 Type II certified). De-duplication was applied at the custodian level using MD5 hash values, with a subsequent cross-custodian de-duplication pass applied after all custodian collections were completed. De-NISTing was applied to remove known system and application files using the National Institute of Standards and Technology\'s National Software Reference Library hash sets. Date culling was applied consistent with the subpoena\'s January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023 time frame, based on the \"last modified date\" for loose files and \"date sent\" for email items.
74	
75	**Quality Assurance.** Stratton performed sample-level quality assurance checks at each stage of the collection and processing workflow, including verification of forensic image integrity, spot-check comparison of extracted email counts against source mailbox counts, review of processing exception reports for corrupted or unprocessable files, and validation of ingested document counts in Relativity. Exception reports were generated at each stage and provided to HRK\'s project management team. Any material discrepancies identified during QA are noted in the custodian-specific sections and in Section 7 below.
76	
77	**[Section 4: Custodian-by-Custodian Collection Details]{.underline}**
78	
79	**4.1 Garrett Whitford --- Managing Partner, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC**
80	
81	**Corporate Email (Outlook / Exchange Online).** Mr. Whitford\'s corporate email account (gwhitford@ridgelinecapital.com) was collected on January 28, 2025 via remote journal extraction from Ridgeline\'s Microsoft 365 tenant. The collection encompassed Mr. Whitford\'s primary mailbox, sent items folder, deleted items folder (including recoverable deleted items), and online archive mailbox. The date range filter of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023 was applied at extraction. Total items extracted: 23,847 email items (prior to de-duplication and de-NISTing). Following processing, 18,612 unique items were ingested into Relativity and made available for review.
82	
83	**Laptop (Ridgeline-Issued Dell Latitude 5530).** Mr. Whitford\'s corporate laptop, a Dell Latitude 5530 (Ridgeline Asset Tag RL-IT-0412, Serial No. DELLSVCTAG-7842), was forensically imaged on January 29, 2025 at Ridgeline\'s offices at 595 Madison Avenue, 22nd Floor, New York, NY. The imaging was performed by Stratton forensic examiner David Parrish using write-blocking hardware and FTK Imager. SHA-256 hash verification was completed successfully. Total raw data on the device was approximately 287 GB. After processing (de-NISTing, date culling, and de-duplication against email), 4,211 unique documents were ingested into Relativity.
84	
85	**Personal Mobile Device (Apple iPhone 15 Pro).**
86	
87	**CRITICAL EXCEPTION ---** Stratton was authorized by HRK to collect Mr. Whitford\'s personal Apple iPhone 15 Pro on February 3, 2025. Mr. Whitford presented the device to Stratton\'s forensic examiner at Stratton\'s New York office. Upon intake and preliminary examination, Stratton\'s forensic examiner determined that the device had been **factory reset on or about January 20, 2025** --- approximately **six (6) days after the Grand Jury Subpoena was issued on January 14, 2025**. The factory reset was confirmed via iOS diagnostic logs recovered during the Cellebrite extraction attempt. Specifically, the iOS Analytics and Diagnostics log data, partially recoverable from residual system partitions, indicated an \"Erase All Content and Settings\" event with a timestamp of January 20, 2025 at approximately 2:47 PM Eastern Standard Time.
88	
89	As a result of the factory reset, **no Signal application data** and **no WhatsApp application data** were recoverable from the device. Both applications had reportedly been installed on the device prior to the reset. Mr. Whitford\'s custodial questionnaire response, completed on January 24, 2025 and provided to Stratton by HRK, states that Mr. Whitford \"occasionally used Signal and WhatsApp for business communications\" on his personal iPhone during the relevant time period. The questionnaire did not elaborate on the frequency, recipients, or subject matter of those communications.
90	
91	**iMessage Extraction:** iMessage data was partially recovered --- not from the device itself (which had been wiped), but from Mr. Whitford\'s **iCloud account backup**. Stratton accessed the iCloud backup with Mr. Whitford\'s written authorization (dated February 3, 2025). The most recent iCloud backup predating the factory reset was dated **January 18, 2025**. This backup contained iMessage conversation threads, which Stratton extracted and processed. A total of 1,247 iMessage items were recovered from this backup source. However, any iMessage threads created, sent, or received between January 18, 2025 (the date of the last iCloud backup) and January 20, 2025 (the date of the factory reset) are unrecoverable, as those messages were not captured in any backup prior to the device wipe.
92	
93	**Signal Data:** Signal uses end-to-end encryption and, by design, does not store message content in iCloud backups. Signal\'s architecture requires that message data be extracted directly from the device on which the application is installed. Because the device was factory reset, Signal message data is entirely unrecoverable from this device. Stratton is not aware of any linked Signal desktop application or secondary device associated with Mr. Whitford that could serve as an alternative source.
94	
95	**WhatsApp Data:** The iCloud backup configuration recovered from the January 18, 2025 backup indicated that WhatsApp\'s \"Chat Backup\" feature was set to **\"Off.\"** This means WhatsApp message data was not included in Mr. Whitford\'s iCloud backups. WhatsApp also permits backup to Google Drive on Android devices, but Mr. Whitford\'s device was an iPhone and no Google Drive backup of WhatsApp was identified. Accordingly, **WhatsApp communications from Mr. Whitford\'s device are entirely unrecoverable.**
96	
97	The collection summary for this device records the unavailability of Signal and WhatsApp data as \"claimed unavailability --- device factory reset prior to collection.\" Stratton informed Jordan Tavares of HRK of this finding via telephone on February 4, 2025 and followed up with a written notification (email from Allison Bray to Jordan Tavares) on February 5, 2025.
98	
99	Total items from personal device (iMessage only, via iCloud backup): **1,247 items** ingested into Relativity.
100	
101	**Whitford Subtotal:** **24,070 unique items** ingested across all sources (after de-duplication).
102	
103	**4.2 Diana Cheng-Rourke --- Partner, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC**
104	
105	**Corporate Email (Outlook / Exchange Online).** Ms. Cheng-Rourke\'s corporate email account (dchengrourke@ridgelinecapital.com) was collected on January 28, 2025 via the same remote journal extraction methodology used for Mr. Whitford, from Ridgeline\'s Microsoft 365 tenant. The collection encompassed Ms. Cheng-Rourke\'s primary mailbox, sent items, deleted items (including recoverable deleted items), and online archive. The date range filter of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023 was applied. Total items extracted: 19,433 email items. Following processing: **15,287 unique items** ingested into Relativity.
106	
107	**Laptop (Ridgeline-Issued Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon).** Ms. Cheng-Rourke\'s corporate laptop, a Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon (Ridgeline Asset Tag RL-IT-0538, Serial No. LNVO-X1C-29174), was forensically imaged on January 30, 2025 at Ridgeline\'s offices. SHA-256 hash verification was completed successfully. Total raw data: approximately 194 GB. After processing: **3,018 unique documents** ingested into Relativity.
108	
109	**Personal Mobile Device (Apple iPhone 14 Pro).** Ms. Cheng-Rourke\'s personal Apple iPhone 14 Pro was made available for collection on February 5, 2025. A physical extraction was performed via Cellebrite UFED at Stratton\'s New York office.
110	
111	> •**iMessage:** Successfully extracted. 2,814 iMessage items were recovered within the date range of January 2019 through December 2023.
112	>
113	> •**WhatsApp:** Successfully extracted. 1,672 WhatsApp messages were recovered from the device\'s local application database. WhatsApp was actively backed up to iCloud on this device; for completeness, Stratton performed extraction from both the device and the iCloud backup and de-duplicated the results.
114	>
115	> •**Signal:** Ms. Cheng-Rourke confirmed during her custodial interview that Signal was **not installed** on her personal device during the relevant period and is not currently installed on the device. No Signal application data was recovered. This representation is consistent with Stratton\'s device analysis, which found no record of Signal in the device\'s application installation history at any point during or after the relevant time period.
116	
117	No exceptions or material issues were noted for this custodian\'s collection. All identified data sources were successfully imaged and extracted.
118	
119	**Cheng-Rourke Subtotal:** **22,791 unique items** ingested across all sources (after de-duplication).
120	
121	**4.3 Tobias Krell --- Vice President, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC**
122	
123	**Corporate Email (Outlook / Exchange Online).** Mr. Krell\'s corporate email account (tkrell@ridgelinecapital.com) was collected on January 28, 2025 via remote journal extraction from Ridgeline\'s Microsoft 365 tenant. The collection encompassed Mr. Krell\'s primary mailbox, sent items, deleted items (including recoverable deleted items), and online archive. Date range filter: January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023. Total items extracted: 14,892 email items. Following processing: **11,544 unique items** ingested into Relativity.
124	
125	**Laptop (Ridgeline-Issued Dell Latitude 5540).** Mr. Krell\'s corporate laptop, a Dell Latitude 5540 (Ridgeline Asset Tag RL-IT-0621, Serial No. DELLSVCTAG-9023), was forensically imaged on January 30, 2025 at Ridgeline\'s offices. SHA-256 hash verification was completed successfully. Total raw data: approximately 162 GB. After processing: **2,647 unique documents** ingested into Relativity.
126	
127	**Personal Mobile Device (Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra).** Mr. Krell\'s personal Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra was made available for collection on February 6, 2025. A logical extraction was performed via Cellebrite UFED at Stratton\'s New York office.
128	
129	> •**iMessage:** Not applicable --- Mr. Krell\'s device is an Android device and does not support Apple\'s iMessage protocol. SMS/MMS messages were extracted in lieu of iMessage. A total of 487 SMS/MMS items within the relevant date range were recovered.
130	>
131	> •**WhatsApp:** Successfully extracted. 2,319 WhatsApp messages were recovered from the local application database on the device.
132	>
133	> •**Signal:** Successfully extracted. 894 Signal messages were recovered from the local application database. Stratton notes that Signal\'s \"disappearing messages\" feature was enabled for certain conversation threads on Mr. Krell\'s device. Messages that had self-deleted in accordance with the application\'s timer settings prior to the date of extraction (February 6, 2025) are not recoverable. However, all messages present on the device at the time of extraction were captured in full. The disappearing messages feature is a standard Signal application function controlled by conversation participants, and its activation does not constitute a collection failure.
134	
135	No material exceptions were noted for this custodian\'s collection. The disappearing messages feature in Signal is noted for counsel\'s awareness and is discussed further in Section 7.6 below.
136	
137	**Krell Subtotal:** **17,891 unique items** ingested across all sources (after de-duplication).
138	
139	**4.4 Dr. Priya Anand --- Former CEO, MedCore Diagnostics Inc. (2020--2022)**
140	
141	**Preliminary Note on Representation.** Dr. Priya Anand is represented by separate, independent counsel --- Miriam Solano of Wren & Kessler LLP, 210 West Street, Suite 1800, New York, NY 10013. Dr. Anand is not represented by HRK. Accordingly, all collection activities involving Dr. Anand\'s personal accounts and personal devices require coordination with and affirmative consent from Dr. Anand\'s independent counsel. As of the date of this report, certain collection activities involving Dr. Anand\'s personal data sources remain incomplete due to ongoing negotiations between HRK and Dr. Anand\'s counsel, as detailed below.
142	
143	**Corporate Email (MedCore Diagnostics Exchange).** Dr. Anand\'s MedCore corporate email account (pranand@medcorediagnostics.com) was collected on February 10, 2025. MedCore\'s IT department, now operating under Veriton Health Systems\' ownership and IT governance, provided administrative access to Dr. Anand\'s archived corporate mailbox, which had been retained in MedCore\'s Exchange environment following Dr. Anand\'s departure in November 2022. The collection encompassed the full mailbox contents. Total items extracted: 8,944 email items. Following processing (de-NISTing, date culling, de-duplication): **7,122 unique items** ingested into Relativity.
144	
145	**MedCore-Issued Laptop.** The corporate laptop assigned to Dr. Anand during her tenure at MedCore was returned to MedCore\'s IT department upon her departure in November 2022. Veriton\'s IT department confirmed that the laptop was subsequently wiped and redeployed to another Veriton employee as part of Veriton\'s standard IT asset refresh policy implemented in the first quarter of 2023. The laptop is no longer available for forensic imaging, and its contents were not separately preserved or backed up prior to the wipe. Veriton\'s IT Director, Sean Nakamura, confirmed this in writing to HRK on February 12, 2025. It is anticipated that the majority of Dr. Anand\'s document-based work product would be captured through corporate email and network file shares; however, any locally stored files that were not also saved to corporate repositories or transmitted via email are unrecoverable.
146	
147	**Personal Email (Gmail Account --- pranand.personal@gmail.com).**
148	
149	**CRITICAL EXCEPTION ---** During the custodial interview conducted by HRK on January 31, 2025, Dr. Anand acknowledged using a **personal Gmail account** (pranand.personal@gmail.com) for certain business-related communications during her tenure as CEO of MedCore. Dr. Anand indicated that she \"occasionally forwarded documents to her personal account for review at home\" and \"used personal email for scheduling and some communications with consultants.\" Dr. Anand further stated that she communicated with Ridgeline personnel, MedCore board members, and certain MedCore employees via this personal Gmail account on an intermittent basis, though she characterized her primary mode of business communication as her MedCore corporate email.
150	
151	As of the date of this report, **Dr. Anand\'s personal Gmail account has not been collected.** Dr. Anand\'s independent counsel, Miriam Solano, has indicated that collection of the personal Gmail account requires further negotiation regarding: (i) the permissible scope of the collection (i.e., whether the entire account must be collected or whether keyword or date-range filtering can be applied at the point of extraction); (ii) privilege protections, including attorney-client communications between Dr. Anand and her own counsel that may reside in the account; and (iii) the terms under which personal, non-business communications would be identified, segregated, and protected from disclosure.
152	
153	Stratton prepared a detailed collection protocol proposal for Dr. Anand\'s personal Gmail account, which was transmitted by HRK to Ms. Solano on March 5, 2025. The proposed protocol included date-range filtering (January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023), collection via Google Takeout with Dr. Anand\'s written authorization, and a privilege-review workflow that would allow Dr. Anand\'s counsel to review the collected materials for privilege and personal-content designations prior to ingestion into the Relativity review database. As of April 8, 2025, no substantive response to this proposal has been received from Dr. Anand\'s counsel.
154	
155	This collection gap is noted as **potentially material** given Dr. Anand\'s role as CEO of MedCore during the entire Ridgeline ownership period (March 2020 through November 2022) and her designation as one of only four named custodians in the subpoena. The personal Gmail account may contain documents responsive to multiple subpoena request categories, including but not limited to: Request 2 (communications regarding MedCore\'s revenue, financial performance, and projections); Request 3 (FDA regulatory submissions and correspondence, including the VeriScan Pro 510(k)); Request 8 (financial statements and audited financials); Request 9 (complaints, concerns, or whistleblower reports regarding MedCore\'s products, testing data, or regulatory compliance); and Request 14 (management compensation, bonus, and incentive arrangements).
156	
157	**Personal Mobile Device (Apple iPhone 13).**
158	
159	**CRITICAL EXCEPTION ---** Dr. Anand\'s personal mobile device, an Apple iPhone 13, has **not been collected.** Dr. Anand\'s independent counsel has not consented to forensic extraction of the device. Ms. Solano has raised concerns regarding the breadth of a forensic extraction, the privacy implications of capturing non-business personal communications and data, and the scope of data that a Cellebrite or GrayKey extraction would capture beyond the messaging applications specifically identified in the subpoena.
160	
161	Stratton prepared a targeted extraction protocol designed to address these concerns, which was included in the March 5, 2025 submission to Dr. Anand\'s counsel. The proposed targeted protocol would limit the extraction to: (i) iMessage conversations; (ii) WhatsApp local application database; (iii) Signal local application database (if installed); and (iv) SMS/MMS messages --- in each case, further limited to communications with a specified list of contact phone numbers corresponding to the other three custodians and key MedCore and Ridgeline personnel (a total of twelve specified contact numbers). This approach would exclude personal photographs, browsing history, location data, and communications with non-specified contacts. No response to this proposal has been received as of the date of this report.
162	
163	Dr. Anand\'s personal phone is potentially responsive to Request 15 of the subpoena (which specifically calls for personal devices and messaging application communications among custodians and key personnel) and may contain communications responsive to other request categories as well. It is unknown at this time whether Dr. Anand used Signal, WhatsApp, or other encrypted or ephemeral messaging applications for business purposes during her tenure at MedCore. This could not be confirmed absent a device examination, a review of the device\'s application installation history, or a supplemental custodial questionnaire response. A supplemental questionnaire was transmitted to Dr. Anand\'s counsel on March 5, 2025 but has not been returned.
164	
165	**Anand Subtotal:** **7,122 unique items** ingested into Relativity (MedCore corporate email only). Dr. Anand\'s personal Gmail account and personal mobile device remain uncollected.
166	
167	**[Section 5: Non-Custodial Sources]{.underline}**
168	
169	**5.1 Ridgeline Capital Partners --- Corporate Network and Shared Drives**
170	
171	**Corporate File Server.** Ridgeline\'s corporate file server, mapped as the \"R:\\\" drive at the 595 Madison Avenue office and hosted on a Windows Server 2019 environment, was forensically imaged on February 3, 2025. Stratton, working with Ridgeline\'s IT Director Mark Ellison, identified and collected the following relevant folder paths: \"R:\\Deal Files\\MedCore,\" \"R:\\Fund III\\Portfolio Companies\\MedCore,\" \"R:\\Investor Relations\\Fund III Reports,\" and \"R:\\Legal\\MedCore.\" Total data collected from these folder paths was approximately 48 GB. After processing (de-NISTing, date culling, de-duplication against custodian email and laptop collections): **8,219 unique documents** were ingested into Relativity.
172	
173	**Ridgeline SharePoint --- \"MedCore Deal Team\" Site.** The \"MedCore Deal Team\" SharePoint site within Ridgeline\'s Microsoft 365 tenant was identified during scoping and collected on February 7, 2025 via SharePoint Online export. This site contained deal-related working documents, including due diligence materials, financial models, and internal memoranda. After processing: **1,844 unique documents** ingested into Relativity.
174	
175	**EXCEPTION --- MedCore Board --- Corporate Secretary SharePoint Site.** A separate SharePoint site identified as **\"MedCore Board --- Corporate Secretary\"** was identified during the scoping process as containing MedCore board of directors meeting materials, including meeting minutes, board resolutions, board information packages, and related attachments. This site was maintained by MedCore\'s corporate secretary during the Ridgeline ownership period and is hosted on MedCore\'s SharePoint tenant --- which is now part of Veriton Health Systems\' Microsoft 365 environment, not Ridgeline\'s.
176	
177	During scoping interviews, Ridgeline\'s corporate secretary, Elaine Marchetti, confirmed that **MedCore board minutes for all quarters during the Ridgeline ownership period (Q2 2020 through Q3 2022)** were maintained exclusively on this SharePoint site. Ms. Marchetti specifically noted that board minutes for **Q3 2021** (covering the board meeting held in approximately September or October 2021) and **Q1 2022** (covering the board meeting held in approximately January or February 2022) were stored exclusively on this site and were **not duplicated** in any Ridgeline-side repository, in any custodian\'s email account, or on the Ridgeline corporate file server. Board minutes for other quarters may have been partially duplicated through email distribution, but the Q3 2021 and Q1 2022 minutes were confirmed as existing only on this SharePoint site.
178	
179	As of the date of this report, **this SharePoint site has not been collected.** Access to the site requires coordination with Veriton Health Systems\' IT department, as the site is hosted on Veriton\'s Microsoft 365 tenant and is subject to Veriton\'s access controls. HRK has submitted a formal access request through Veriton\'s outside counsel, Preston & Gage LLP, on March 12, 2025. Stratton is prepared to perform the collection upon receiving access credentials and authorization to proceed.
180	
181	The absence of this collection means that board minutes for Q3 2021 and Q1 2022 --- and any associated board information packages, which typically include quarterly financial reports, operational updates, regulatory status summaries, and management presentations --- are **not included** in the current document population available for review and production. These materials are potentially responsive to multiple subpoena request categories, most directly Request 7 (board minutes and board packages), and also likely Requests 2 (revenue and financial performance data typically included in board packages), 3 (FDA regulatory updates that would have been presented to the board), 8 (financial statements appended to board packages), and 18 (valuation materials presented to the board).
182	
183	The Q3 2021 board meeting is of particular significance because it would have occurred approximately one to two months after the submission of MedCore\'s VeriScan Pro FDA 510(k) application (designated MC-510k-2021-04, submitted in June 2021), and approximately contemporaneously with the date of the August 14, 2021 email from former MedCore Quality Assurance Director Marcus Webb to Diana Cheng-Rourke, which is referenced in HRK\'s custodian interview notes and which Stratton understands to be a document of particular interest in the investigation. Board discussion of VeriScan Pro testing data, quality concerns, or regulatory status during this period is reasonably foreseeable, and the absence of the Q3 2021 board minutes from the reviewable population represents a material gap.
184	
185	**5.2 MedCore Diagnostics --- Corporate Systems**
186	
187	**MedCore Corporate Email (Exchange).** MedCore\'s corporate email environment was accessed with the cooperation of Veriton Health Systems\' IT department. Collections from this environment were limited to the archived mailboxes of the four designated custodians. Among the four custodians, only Dr. Anand maintained a MedCore corporate email account; the three Ridgeline custodians communicated with MedCore personnel through their Ridgeline email accounts and did not have MedCore-domain accounts. Dr. Anand\'s MedCore email collection is described in Section 4.4 above.
188	
189	**MedCore Documentum Document Management System.** During the scoping process, Stratton identified that MedCore maintained an OpenText Documentum-based document management system (\"DMS\") for its regulatory, quality assurance, and compliance documentation. This DMS is believed to be the primary repository for the following categories of documents:
190	
191	> •FDA 510(k) submissions and related correspondence, including application MC-510k-2021-04 (VeriScan Pro) and application MC-510k-2022-01 (CoreAssay Plus);
192	>
193	> •Internal regulatory assessment memoranda and pre-submission analyses;
194	>
195	> •Quality assurance reports, testing protocols, testing data, and validation studies;
196	>
197	> •Compliance review documentation, including internal audit reports and corrective action records.
198	
199	**The MedCore Documentum DMS has not been collected as of the date of this report.** Veriton Health Systems\' IT department has confirmed that the Documentum system remains operational and accessible within Veriton\'s IT environment, but any export or collection from the system requires formal approval from Veriton\'s legal department and may require technical assistance from Veriton\'s IT staff to configure and execute the export. Stratton communicated this gap to HRK via email from Allison Bray to Jordan Tavares dated March 28, 2025, and recommended that HRK pursue access through Veriton\'s outside counsel.
200	
201	The absence of this collection is directly relevant to the subpoena\'s Request 3 (FDA 510(k) applications, submissions, and related correspondence), Request 9 (complaints, concerns, or whistleblower reports regarding product quality, safety, or regulatory compliance), and Request 16 (internal investigations, compliance reviews, and audit reports).
202	
203	**MedCore Network File Shares (Partial Collection).** MedCore\'s legacy network file shares were partially collected. Veriton\'s IT department provided Stratton with access to archived MedCore shared drive folders covering the following departments and subject areas: Finance, Executive Office, and Deal/Sale Process (i.e., the folders related to the Veriton acquisition). Access was provided on February 14, 2025, and the collection was completed on February 17, 2025. Total data collected: approximately 22 GB. After processing: **4,188 unique documents** ingested into Relativity. Notably, Regulatory Affairs department folders, Quality Assurance department folders, and Research & Development department folders were **not included** in this partial collection. Veriton\'s IT department indicated that these folders could be made available in a subsequent collection phase upon legal authorization.
204	
205	**5.3 Third-Party Sources**
206	
207	**Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co. HRK issued a document preservation request and third-party subpoena to Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co., the investment bank that served as financial advisor on the MedCore sale transaction in 2022. Stratton has not been engaged to perform collections from Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn, and any document productions from Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn will be handled separately by HRK. Stratton notes this for completeness and to confirm that Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn materials are not included in the current Relativity population.**
208	
209	**Adler, Connolly & Strauss LLP.** HRK has coordinated with Adler, Connolly & Strauss LLP (\"ACS\"), Ridgeline\'s prior outside counsel for the MedCore acquisition transaction in 2020 and certain ongoing corporate matters during the ownership period, regarding preservation and potential production of relevant files maintained in ACS\'s records. Stratton has not been engaged to collect from ACS; counsel-to-counsel negotiations regarding scope and logistics are ongoing.
210	
211	**Pennfield & Associates LLP.** Pennfield & Associates LLP served as MedCore\'s outside auditor during the Ridgeline ownership period. No collection has been undertaken from Pennfield. HRK has indicated that Pennfield may be a second-phase collection target for audit workpapers and related materials potentially responsive to Request 8.
212	
213	**Thorngate Valuation Group.** Thorngate Valuation Group was the third-party valuation firm engaged by Ridgeline for quarterly portfolio company fair market value assessments, including quarterly marks for MedCore. No collection has been undertaken from Thorngate. HRK has indicated that Thorngate may be a second-phase collection target for valuation reports and supporting analyses potentially responsive to Request 18.

259	**[Section 7: Issues, Exceptions, and Recommendations]{.underline}**
260	
261	This section consolidates all collection issues and exceptions identified during the engagement, cross-referencing the custodian-specific and source-specific discussions in Sections 4 and 5 above, and provides Stratton\'s recommendations to counsel. Issues are categorized by priority level.
262	
263	**7.1 Garrett Whitford --- Personal Device Factory Reset (HIGH PRIORITY)**
264	
265	**.** As detailed in Section 4.1, Mr. Whitford\'s personal Apple iPhone 15 Pro was factory reset on January 20, 2025, approximately six days after the Grand Jury Subpoena was issued on January 14, 2025. The factory reset was confirmed by iOS diagnostic log data indicating an \"Erase All Content and Settings\" event at approximately 2:47 PM EST on that date.
266	
267	As a consequence of the factory reset:
268	
269	> •**Signal data** from Mr. Whitford\'s device is **entirely unrecoverable**. Signal does not back up message content to iCloud.
270	>
271	> •**WhatsApp data** from Mr. Whitford\'s device is **entirely unrecoverable**. WhatsApp\'s iCloud chat backup was set to \"Off\" on the device.
272	>
273	> •**iMessage data** was only **partially recovered** from an iCloud backup dated January 18, 2025 --- two days before the reset. Any iMessage communications between January 18, 2025 and January 20, 2025 are unrecoverable.
274	
275	Mr. Whitford acknowledged in his custodial questionnaire response, dated January 24, 2025, that he \"occasionally used Signal and WhatsApp for business communications\" on this device.
276	
277	The chronological proximity of the factory reset (January 20, 2025) to the issuance of the Grand Jury Subpoena (January 14, 2025) raises significant preservation concerns that counsel should evaluate carefully.
278	
279	**Recommendations:** Stratton recommends that HRK:
280	
281	> \(a\) Consult with Mr. Whitford regarding the specific circumstances, purpose, and timing of the factory reset;
282	>
283	> \(b\) Determine whether any additional backup sources may exist for Signal or WhatsApp data, including but not limited to: WhatsApp backup to Google Drive (unlikely for an iPhone user, but worth confirming), Signal transfer or backup to a linked desktop device, carrier records for SMS/MMS (which would not capture Signal or WhatsApp content but could identify communication patterns), and any other Apple devices linked to Mr. Whitford\'s iCloud account that might contain synced iMessage data;
284	>
285	> \(c\) Evaluate disclosure obligations to the U.S. Attorney\'s Office with respect to the factory reset and resulting data loss, including whether affirmative disclosure is required or advisable; and
286	>
287	> \(d\) Consider whether additional forensic recovery from the iCloud account is technically feasible, including examination of deleted-but-recoverable items in iCloud storage or identification of other synced Apple devices (e.g., iPad, MacBook) that may contain copies of iMessage conversations.
288	
289	**7.2 Dr. Priya Anand --- Uncollected Personal Gmail Account (HIGH PRIORITY)**
290	
291	**.** As detailed in Section 4.4, Dr. Anand\'s personal Gmail account (pranand.personal@gmail.com) has been identified as containing business-related communications from her tenure as CEO of MedCore, including correspondence with Ridgeline personnel, board members, MedCore employees, and consultants. Despite Dr. Anand\'s own acknowledgment of business use during her January 31, 2025 custodial interview, the account has not been collected. Negotiations with Dr. Anand\'s independent counsel (Miriam Solano, Wren & Kessler LLP) have been ongoing since March 5, 2025, when HRK transmitted Stratton\'s proposed collection protocol. No substantive response has been received as of April 8, 2025.
292	
293	**Recommendation:** Stratton recommends that HRK escalate this issue with Dr. Anand\'s counsel on an expedited basis, given the approaching April 15, 2025 first rolling production date. The uncollected Gmail account may contain documents responsive to multiple subpoena request categories (Requests 2, 3, 8, 9, and 14, among others). If consent is not forthcoming within a reasonable timeframe, counsel should evaluate whether to seek judicial assistance (e.g., a motion to compel), negotiate directly with the U.S. Attorney\'s Office regarding the collection gap, or inform the government of the outstanding item in connection with the rolling production.
294	
295	**7.3 Dr. Priya Anand --- Uncollected Personal Mobile Device (HIGH PRIORITY)**
296	
297	**.** As detailed in Section 4.4, Dr. Anand\'s personal Apple iPhone 13 has not been collected due to non-consent from her independent counsel. The scope of messaging application usage (Signal, WhatsApp, iMessage) during the relevant period is unknown and could not be confirmed absent a device examination or a supplemental custodial questionnaire response, which has been requested but not returned.
298	
299	**Recommendation:** Stratton\'s recommendations mirror those set forth in Section 7.2 above. Stratton\'s proposed targeted extraction protocol --- limited to iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, and SMS/MMS communications with twelve specified contact numbers --- remains available and is designed to minimize privacy concerns while ensuring responsive data is captured. HRK should press for a response from Dr. Anand\'s counsel and, if necessary, consider the same escalation options described above.
300	
301	**7.4 MedCore Board --- Corporate Secretary SharePoint Site (HIGH PRIORITY)**
302	
303	**.** As detailed in Section 5.1, the \"MedCore Board --- Corporate Secretary\" SharePoint site, hosted on Veriton Health Systems\' Microsoft 365 tenant, has not been collected. This site is confirmed to contain board of directors meeting minutes and information packages for all quarters during the Ridgeline ownership period, including Q3 2021 and Q1 2022 materials that are **known to exist exclusively on this site** and are not duplicated in any other collected source.
304	
305	These materials are responsive to multiple subpoena categories, most directly Request 7 (board minutes and packages) and also Requests 2, 3, 8, and 18. The Q3 2021 board meeting is of particular significance given its temporal proximity to the VeriScan Pro 510(k) submission (June 2021) and the August 14, 2021 Marcus Webb email.
306	
307	**Recommendation:** Stratton recommends that HRK authorize immediate coordination with Veriton Health Systems\' IT department, through Veriton\'s outside counsel, to obtain access to this SharePoint site. Upon receiving access credentials and authorization, Stratton can perform the collection within five to seven business days. Given the significance of these materials, Stratton recommends prioritizing this collection ahead of other second-phase items.
308	
309	**7.5 MedCore Documentum DMS (MEDIUM-HIGH PRIORITY)**
310	
311	The MedCore Documentum document management system, housing MedCore\'s regulatory, quality assurance, and compliance documentation, has not been collected. This system is the likely primary repository for FDA 510(k) application files and supporting materials (responsive to Request 3), quality assurance reports and testing data, and compliance review documentation (potentially responsive to Requests 9 and 16). The system remains operational within Veriton\'s IT environment but requires Veriton legal approval for export.
312	
313	**Recommendation:** Stratton recommends that HRK pursue access to the Documentum system through Veriton\'s outside counsel as a priority supplemental collection. Stratton has substantial experience with Documentum-based exports and can provide a detailed technical collection plan, including estimated timelines and data volumes, upon authorization from HRK. Given the regulatory focus of several subpoena request categories, this collection should be treated as a high-priority item for the second phase.
314	
315	**7.6 Other Noted Items (LOWER PRIORITY)**
316	
317	**Dr. Anand\'s MedCore Laptop.** As noted in Section 4.4, Dr. Anand\'s MedCore-issued laptop was wiped and redeployed by Veriton\'s IT department in the first quarter of 2023 as part of Veriton\'s standard asset refresh policy. This data loss occurred before the subpoena was issued (January 14, 2025) and before Stratton\'s engagement (January 22, 2025). It does not appear to represent a preservation failure attributable to Ridgeline. However, counsel should evaluate whether Veriton\'s actions are relevant in the context of the government\'s investigation and whether any notification to the government is appropriate.

Collections from third-party sources --- specifically Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co., Adler, Connolly & Strauss LLP, Pennfield & Associates LLP, and Thorngate Valuation Group --- have not been undertaken by Stratton and may be needed for comprehensive subpoena compliance. Stratton is available to perform collections from these sources upon HRK\'s authorization and the resolution of any access or consent issues.**

However, counsel should be aware that the Signal messages recovered from Mr. Krell\'s device may represent an incomplete record of Signal communications for threads where disappearing messages were active.

27	**[II. Background and Role at Ridgeline Capital Partners]{.underline}**
28	
29	Diana Cheng-Rourke is forty-four years old and is currently a Partner at Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC, where she heads the Healthcare Vertical. She joined Ridgeline in 2016, initially in the role of Principal, and was promoted to Partner in 2018. Prior to joining Ridgeline, she spent approximately eight years in prior roles in healthcare investment banking and consulting, where she developed subject-matter expertise in the healthcare and life sciences sectors. She holds an MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania and a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Duke University.
30	
31	Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC is a Delaware limited liability company formed in 2014. It is headquartered at 595 Madison Avenue, 22nd Floor, New York, NY 10022. Ridgeline manages approximately \$2.8 billion in assets under management across three active fund vehicles: Ridgeline Capital Fund II LP, Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP, and Ridgeline Capital Fund IV LP. The firm\'s investment strategy focuses on middle-market companies across several verticals, including healthcare, technology-enabled services, and specialty industrials.
32	
33	In her capacity as head of the Healthcare Vertical, Ms. Cheng-Rourke is responsible for sourcing and evaluating healthcare investment opportunities, leading due diligence on prospective healthcare targets, overseeing post-acquisition management and value creation at healthcare portfolio companies, and representing Ridgeline on the boards of directors of healthcare portfolio companies. She described her role as encompassing both the transactional and operational phases of Ridgeline\'s healthcare investments.
34	
35	Ms. Cheng-Rourke was the senior deal team member responsible for the MedCore Diagnostics Inc. investment. She worked alongside Managing Partner Garrett Whitford, who maintained overarching responsibility for fund-level investment decisions. The specific fund vehicle that held the MedCore investment was Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP.
36	
37	**[III. MedCore Diagnostics --- Acquisition Phase]{.underline}**
38	
39	Ms. Cheng-Rourke described in detail her involvement in the acquisition of MedCore Diagnostics Inc. MedCore Diagnostics Inc. is a Delaware corporation with its principal offices located at 2100 Lakewood Boulevard, Suite 400, Durham, North Carolina 27703. MedCore is engaged in the manufacture and distribution of in-vitro diagnostic (\"IVD\") testing equipment, serving hospitals, clinical laboratories, and reference laboratories across the United States.
40	
41	According to Ms. Cheng-Rourke, Ridgeline first evaluated MedCore as a potential acquisition target in approximately mid-2019. The company was identified through the firm\'s proprietary deal sourcing process within the healthcare vertical. Ridgeline was attracted to MedCore\'s strong position in the IVD space, its established revenue base (fiscal year 2019 revenue of approximately \$78 million), and what Ms. Cheng-Rourke described as a \"compelling growth profile\" driven by the expansion of diagnostic testing volumes and the introduction of new product platforms.
42	
43	A formal due diligence process was conducted from approximately October 2019 through February 2020. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she reviewed financial diligence materials, including audited financial statements and management-prepared financial projections. She also reviewed quality systems documentation related to MedCore\'s manufacturing processes and regulatory filings, including existing FDA clearances and the regulatory pathway for MedCore\'s product pipeline. She noted that the diligence process was conducted in collaboration with Ridgeline\'s internal team and outside advisors.
44	
45	The acquisition of MedCore Diagnostics closed on March 15, 2020, at a total purchase price of \$185 million. Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP invested \$92.5 million in equity, representing fifty percent of the purchase price; the remaining \$92.5 million was funded through debt financing arranged at closing. Ms. Cheng-Rourke described the transaction structure as a leveraged buyout, consistent with Ridgeline\'s standard approach for middle-market investments.
46	
47	Following the closing, Ridgeline installed Dr. Priya Anand as Chief Executive Officer of MedCore Diagnostics. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she had worked with Dr. Anand previously on another healthcare portfolio company and recommended her for the CEO role based on Dr. Anand\'s experience in the diagnostics industry and her operational capabilities. The decision to appoint Dr. Anand was made in consultation with Garrett Whitford and was approved by the Ridgeline investment committee.
48	
49	Ms. Cheng-Rourke was appointed to MedCore\'s board of directors in April 2020 and served continuously through the closing of the sale of MedCore in November 2022. She stated that outside counsel for the acquisition was Adler, Connolly & Strauss LLP (\"ACS\"), which handled transactional documentation, regulatory analysis, and some ongoing advisory work post-closing. MedCore\'s outside auditor was Pennfield & Associates LLP, which performed annual audit engagements during the ownership period.

51	**[IV. MedCore Ownership Period --- Board Service and Oversight]{.underline}**
52	
53	Ms. Cheng-Rourke served on the board of directors of MedCore Diagnostics from April 2020 through November 2022, a period of approximately thirty-one months. She described her board service and the cadence of board meetings in detail.
54	
55	The MedCore board met on a quarterly basis. The standard meeting cadence was as follows: Q1 meetings were typically held in March, Q2 meetings in June, Q3 meetings in September, and Q4 meetings in December. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that ad hoc board meetings were also convened as needed to address specific matters requiring board approval or discussion. She recalled that, during her tenure, every quarterly board meeting took place without exception.
56	
57	Board packages were typically prepared by MedCore management --- specifically, Dr. Priya Anand and her executive team --- and circulated to board members via email approximately five to seven days before each meeting. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that the board packages typically included: financial performance summaries (including revenue, EBITDA, and key operating metrics), revenue pipeline updates, regulatory status updates (including the status of FDA submissions and clearances), key customer updates, and a discussion of strategic initiatives. Board meetings were conducted either in person at MedCore\'s Durham offices or via video conference, with the format varying over the course of the ownership period.
58	
59	Board minutes were prepared by MedCore\'s corporate secretary and maintained on a SharePoint site that was separate from MedCore\'s general email systems and separate from Ridgeline\'s own document repositories. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she accessed this SharePoint site to review minutes and board materials on occasion but did not save board minutes locally to her own laptop or Ridgeline network drives.
60	
61	When asked specifically about the Q3 2021 and Q1 2022 board meetings, Ms. Cheng-Rourke confirmed that both meetings took place.
62	
63	Regarding the **Q3 2021 board meeting** (held in approximately September 2021), Ms. Cheng-Rourke recalled this meeting as \"significant\" because it included a discussion of \"testing data validation\" related to MedCore\'s VeriScan Pro rapid testing platform. She recalled Dr. Anand presenting updated accuracy data for the VeriScan Pro platform and stated that there was a \"robust discussion\" at the board level regarding the reliability and validation methodology of the testing data. She believed that Garrett Whitford also attended this meeting, either in person or by video conference. She stated that the board minutes for this meeting would reflect the testing data validation discussion.
64	
65	Regarding the **Q1 2022 board meeting** (held in approximately March 2022), Ms. Cheng-Rourke recalled that this meeting addressed the CoreAssay Plus 510(k) submission (MC-510k-2022-01, which had been submitted to the FDA in February 2022) and included early-stage discussions about a potential sale process for MedCore. She recalled that the board discussed preliminary indications of interest from potential acquirers and the advisability of engaging an investment bank to run a formal process.
66	
67	Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she does not have personal copies of the board minutes from any quarterly meeting. As noted, the board minutes were maintained on MedCore\'s SharePoint site. She was not sure whether those minutes had been collected by the forensic team retained in connection with this matter.

89	**[VI. The Marcus Webb Email --- August 14, 2021]{.underline}**
90	
91	When asked whether she was aware of any complaints, concerns, or quality issues raised by MedCore employees during her tenure as a board member, Ms. Cheng-Rourke recalled receiving an email from Marcus Webb, who at the time served as MedCore\'s Quality Assurance Director.
92	
93	She described the email as arriving on or about August 14, 2021. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she recalled the email clearly because it was unusual for a MedCore employee below the C-suite level to communicate directly with her as a board member.
94	
95	Regarding the content of the email, Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that Webb raised concerns about the reliability of VeriScan Pro testing accuracy data. Specifically, Webb questioned whether certain test results that were being cited internally --- and, as Ms. Cheng-Rourke later acknowledged during the interview, in materials that were subsequently used in the preparation of the Confidential Information Memorandum --- accurately reflected the VeriScan Pro platform\'s actual performance. She described the email as a \"quality concern\" raised by a \"conscientious employee\" who believed the testing data warranted further scrutiny. She recalled that the email was substantive but not excessively long, and that it referenced specific data points or test runs, though she could not recall the precise figures cited.
96	
97	Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that, upon receiving the Webb email, she forwarded it to Dr. Priya Anand, MedCore\'s CEO, and asked Dr. Anand to \"look into it and address it.\" She recalled receiving a response from Dr. Anand --- she was uncertain whether the response came the same day or within a few days --- stating that the concerns were being reviewed and that the data had been validated through MedCore\'s internal protocols. Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she believed, based on Dr. Anand\'s response, that the matter was \"addressed\" by MedCore management.
98	
99	Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that she did not escalate the Webb email further at the time. Specifically, she did not recall raising it formally with the full board of directors, with Garrett Whitford, or with outside counsel at Adler, Connolly & Strauss LLP. She stated that she believed, at the time, that it was appropriate to rely on MedCore management --- and specifically Dr. Anand as CEO --- to evaluate and resolve the quality concern raised by a member of the company\'s quality assurance team.
100

She noted, as described in Section IV above, that the Q3 2021 board meeting included a discussion of \"testing data validation\" related to VeriScan Pro. However, she could not confirm whether that agenda item was directly prompted by the Webb email or arose independently through the normal course of the board\'s oversight of the 510(k) submission process.
102	
103	Ms. Cheng-Rourke stated that Marcus Webb left MedCore \"sometime later.\" She was uncertain of the exact date of his departure but believed it was in late 2021 or early 2022. She did not know whether his departure was voluntary or involuntary, and she stated that she did not have any involvement in or awareness of the circumstances of his departure.
104

185	**Regarding the Webb Email .** The Marcus Webb email dated August 14, 2021, as described by Ms. Cheng-Rourke during the interview, appears squarely responsive to Subpoena Request Category 9. 166	>
167	> 6\. **Follow-Up Interview.** Schedule a follow-up interview with Mr. Krell if review of produced documents raises additional questions about the CIM drafting process, the representations made to Veriton during management presentations, or Mr. Krell\'s awareness of the Webb quality concern.
