26	**[I. INTRODUCTION AND OVERVIEW OF THE MATTER]{.underline}**
27	
28	The purpose of this memorandum is to provide comprehensive coding instructions and responsiveness criteria for the document review being conducted in connection with the Grand Jury Subpoena Duces Tecum issued on January 14, 2025, by the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, Grand Jury No. 24-GJ-0387. The subpoena was served upon Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC and is returnable, as extended by agreement with the United States Attorney\'s Office, on April 15, 2025 (first rolling production) and June 30, 2025 (final production). This memorandum should be read in its entirety before any reviewer begins coding documents. Reviewers are expected to apply the criteria set forth herein consistently and to escalate questions or ambiguities in accordance with the escalation procedures described in Section VII.
29	
30	**Background on the Investigation.** The U.S. Attorney\'s Office for the Southern District of New York, acting through Assistant United States Attorney Bradley Navarro, is investigating potential wire fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1343) and securities fraud (15 U.S.C. § 78j(b); 17 C.F.R. § 240.10b-5) in connection with Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC\'s acquisition and subsequent sale of MedCore Diagnostics Inc. The investigation is being conducted before a federal grand jury empaneled in the Southern District of New York.
31	
32	**Key Transaction Facts.** Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP, a Delaware limited partnership managed by Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC, acquired all of the outstanding equity interests of MedCore Diagnostics Inc.---a Delaware corporation headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, engaged in the design, manufacture, and sale of in-vitro diagnostic testing equipment---on March 15, 2020, for a total purchase price of approximately \$185 million. Following a period of operational management and growth, MedCore was subsequently sold to Veriton Health Systems Inc. on November 18, 2022, for approximately \$410 million, representing a gross return multiple of approximately 2.2x on invested capital.
33	
34	**Government\'s Theory.** Based on our discussions with AUSA Navarro and the language of the subpoena itself, the government\'s investigation centers on allegations that principals of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC made material misrepresentations to the buyer, Veriton Health Systems Inc., regarding MedCore\'s revenue pipeline, revenue recognition practices, and FDA regulatory status during the sale process. In particular, the government appears to be focused on representations made in connection with the Confidential Information Memorandum distributed to prospective buyers and during management presentations conducted prior to closing.
35	
36	**Scope of the Subpoena.** The subpoena contains eighteen (18) numbered request categories spanning the relevant time period of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023. The responsiveness criteria for each request category are set forth in detail in Section III of this memorandum.
37	
38	**Custodians.** Four named custodians have been identified and their documents collected: (1) Garrett Whitford, Managing Partner of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC; (2) Diana Cheng-Rourke, Partner of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC and member of the MedCore Diagnostics Inc. board of directors; (3) Tobias Krell, Vice President of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC; and (4) Dr. Priya Anand, Chief Executive Officer of MedCore Diagnostics Inc. from March 2020 through November 2022.
39	
40	**E-Discovery Vendor and Platform.** Stratton Forensic Consulting LLC (point of contact: Allison Bray) has been retained as the e-discovery vendor for forensic collection, processing, and hosting. All documents are hosted in Relativity, and all coding will be performed within the Relativity platform. Total documents collected and loaded into the review platform number 52,318. The review universe encompasses the full 52,318 documents.
41	
42	**Production Specifications.** The production designation prefix for all documents produced to the government is **RC-PROD-**. Bates numbering will be sequential and applied at the time of production. The negotiated production protocol, memorialized in our February 10, 2025 letter agreement with AUSA Navarro, specifies the production format (single-page TIFF images with extracted or OCR text and a standard Concordance load file), the rolling production schedule, and privilege log requirements. Reviewers should familiarize themselves with the production format specifications to understand how coded documents will ultimately be delivered to the government.
43	
44	**[II. GENERAL REVIEW INSTRUCTIONS]{.underline}**
45	
46	**[II.A. Review Workflow]{.underline}**
47	
48	The document review will proceed in two tiers, followed by a final quality control check prior to each production:
49	
50	**First-Level Review.** All 52,318 documents in the review universe will undergo first-level review for both responsiveness and privilege. Each reviewer will be assigned batches of documents in Relativity according to the batching strategy described in Section VI. Every document must receive a complete set of coding decisions at first-level review --- no document should remain uncoded or partially coded at the conclusion of a reviewer\'s work on a given batch.
51	
52	**Second-Level Review (Quality Control).** All documents coded as responsive will be subject to second-level quality control review to confirm the responsiveness designation and verify the completeness of request category tagging. All documents coded as privileged will undergo second-level privilege review to confirm the privilege designation, assess whether the document can be produced in redacted form rather than withheld in full, and verify completeness of the privilege log entry. Details of the quality control procedures are set forth in Section VIII.
53	
54	**Escalation.** Documents that present coding difficulties, borderline privilege questions, potential sensitivity to the government\'s core theories, or other issues requiring guidance beyond the criteria in this memorandum must be escalated in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section VII. Reviewers should not guess or make assumptions when faced with ambiguous documents. The escalation mechanism exists precisely for these situations, and its use is encouraged.
55	
56	**Coding Fields in Relativity.** The following coding fields have been configured in the Relativity workspace. Reviewers must complete all applicable fields for every document:
57	
58	> 1\. **Responsiveness** --- Single-select: *Responsive* / *Non-Responsive* / *Needs Further Review*. Use \"Needs Further Review\" sparingly and only when escalation is required; this is not a parking designation and should be resolved within the escalation turnaround times specified in Section VII.
59	>
60	> 2\. **Request Category Tags** --- Multi-select: Request Categories 1 through 18. Tag each document to ALL applicable request categories. A single document may be responsive to multiple categories; there is no limit on the number of categories to which a document may be tagged. Do not restrict a document to a single category when it falls within multiple categories.
61	>
62	> 3\. **Privilege Designation** --- Single-select: *Not Privileged* / *Attorney-Client Privilege* / *Work Product* / *Joint Defense Privilege* / *Partial Privilege --- Redact*. If both attorney-client privilege and work product apply to the same document, select the primary basis and note the secondary basis in the free-text field.
63	>
64	> 4\. **Confidentiality** --- Single-select: *Confidential* / *Highly Confidential*. Apply based on the content sensitivity. Documents containing trade secrets, proprietary financial models, or personally identifiable information of non-custodian individuals should generally be designated Highly Confidential.
65	>
66	> 5\. **Redaction Required** --- Single-select: *Yes* / *No*. Mark \"Yes\" if the document requires redaction of privileged content (for partial privilege productions) or of personally identifiable information unrelated to the investigation.
67	>
68	> 6\. **Escalation Flag** --- Single-select: *Yes* / *No* + free-text notes field. When flagging for escalation, include a brief description of the issue necessitating escalation.
69	
70	**Completeness Requirement.** Reviewers must code every document. At no point should a document remain without a responsiveness coding decision. If a reviewer cannot reach a coding decision, the document must be coded \"Needs Further Review\" and flagged for escalation with a note explaining the difficulty.
71	
72	**Multi-Category Tagging.** To reiterate, because this is a frequent source of error: a single document may be --- and often will be --- responsive to multiple request categories. Reviewers must tag all applicable categories. For example, a board package containing financial statements and a discussion of FDA 510(k) status should be tagged to Category 7 (Board Materials), Category 8 (Financial Statements), and Category 3 (FDA 510(k) Materials) at a minimum. Failing to tag all applicable categories undermines the completeness of the production and creates risk for the client.
73	
74	**[II.B. Relevant Time Period]{.underline}**
75	
76	The subpoena defines the relevant time period as **January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2023**. All documents falling within this period should be evaluated against the eighteen request categories for responsiveness.
77	
78	Documents dated outside this period should generally be coded non-responsive. However, documents predating January 1, 2019 or postdating December 31, 2023 should be coded responsive if they are reasonably related to transactions, events, or communications within the relevant period. For example, a preliminary investment analysis or market study prepared in 2018 that directly informed the 2019--2020 acquisition due diligence for MedCore would be responsive notwithstanding its date. Similarly, a January 2024 post-closing indemnification demand referencing events within the relevant period would be responsive.
79	
80	When a document falls outside the relevant time period and the reviewer is uncertain whether it is sufficiently related to events within the period to warrant a responsive coding, the reviewer should code the document as responsive and escalate for secondary review. The preference is to over-include at first-level review and narrow during quality control, rather than risk excluding a potentially responsive document.
81	
82	**[II.C. Document Types]{.underline}**
83	
84	The review universe includes a range of document types collected from the four custodians\' corporate and personal devices and accounts. Document types present in the review platform include:
85	
86	> • **Emails** (including all attachments), collected from Microsoft Outlook accounts and, in the case of Dr. Anand, from a Gmail account used for certain business communications
87	>
88	> • **Instant messages**, including iMessage, WhatsApp, and Signal communications collected from personal devices
89	>
90	> • **Word documents** (.doc, .docx)
91	>
92	> • **Excel spreadsheets** (.xls, .xlsx)
93	>
94	> • **PowerPoint presentations** (.ppt, .pptx)
95	>
96	> • **PDF documents** (native and scanned)
97	>
98	> • **Scanned documents** (processed with OCR by Stratton)
99	>
100	> • **Calendar entries** from Outlook and Google Calendar
101	>
102	> • **Loose electronic files** recovered from forensic laptop images
103	
104	**Email Families.** Reviewers must review the entire email family --- parent email and all attachments --- as a unit. Code the family as a unit. If the parent email is responsive, code the full family as responsive even if individual attachments, standing alone, might not independently meet the responsiveness threshold. Conversely, if only an attachment is responsive but the parent email is not, still code the full family as responsive. Email families should not be split for coding purposes. If different members of an email family implicate different request categories, tag the family to all applicable categories.
105	
106	**Duplicates.** Stratton Forensic Consulting has de-duplicated documents at the custodian level, meaning that if the same document existed in multiple locations within a single custodian\'s data sources, only one instance appears in the review platform. However, cross-custodian duplicates have NOT been de-duplicated. The same document may appear in the review sets of multiple custodians. Each custodian\'s copy must be reviewed and coded independently, because the same document held by different custodians may carry different privilege implications --- for example, a document that is privileged in the hands of one custodian (because it reflects a privileged communication) may not be privileged in the hands of another custodian who received it through non-privileged channels, or vice versa.
107	
108	**[III. RESPONSIVENESS CRITERIA BY REQUEST CATEGORY]{.underline}**
109	
110	This section provides the operative definition of responsiveness for each of the eighteen subpoena request categories. Reviewers should apply these criteria consistently across all custodians and document types. Where the definitions below use quoted language, that language is drawn from or paraphrases the text of the subpoena itself. If a document appears to fall within the plain language of a request category but outside the specific criteria set forth below, the reviewer should escalate the document rather than coding it non-responsive. The goal of this guide is to ensure comprehensive and defensible coding; when in doubt, err on the side of responsiveness and escalate.
111	
112	**[III.A. Request Category 1 --- Acquisition of MedCore]{.underline}**
113	
114	**Responsive:** All documents relating to Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC\'s and Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP\'s acquisition of MedCore Diagnostics Inc., including but not limited to due diligence materials, financial models, term sheets, letters of intent, commitment letters, debt financing documents, equity contribution agreements, and closing documents.
115	
116	**Time Frame Emphasis:** The primary time frame for this category is January 1, 2019 through March 15, 2020 (the acquisition closing date). Documents reflecting pre-acquisition market analysis or target screening that reference MedCore during 2019 are responsive. Documents reflecting post-closing integration matters through the end of 2020 are also responsive to the extent they relate to the acquisition itself (e.g., post-closing purchase price adjustments, earnout calculations, or closing condition satisfaction).
117	
118	**Key Entities:** Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC, Ridgeline Capital Fund III LP, MedCore Diagnostics Inc., and any selling shareholders or entities on the sell-side of the acquisition.
119	
120	**Specific Document Types to Include:** Preliminary investment committee memoranda, management presentations delivered by MedCore\'s prior ownership or management team, third-party due diligence reports (financial, tax, environmental, regulatory, commercial), financial model spreadsheets and projections used to underwrite the acquisition, equity commitment letters, debt financing term sheets and credit agreements, the acquisition agreement (stock purchase agreement or merger agreement) and all ancillary documents, disclosure schedules, closing binders, and funds flow memoranda. Also include any internal Ridgeline communications discussing the merits, risks, or pricing of the acquisition, as well as communications with lenders, co-investors, or advisors in connection with the acquisition.
121	
122	**[III.B. Request Category 2 --- Revenue-Related Communications]{.underline}**
123	
124	**Responsive:** All communications between Ridgeline partners or employees and MedCore management regarding MedCore\'s revenue, revenue projections, revenue forecasts, revenue recognition practices, or revenue-related accounting policies.
125	
126	**Broad Scope:** This category should be interpreted broadly. Include any email, instant message, memorandum, or document that discusses actual revenue figures, revenue forecasts or projections, sales pipeline, order backlog, revenue recognition methodology (including compliance with ASC 606, *Revenue from Contracts with Customers*), and any adjustments, corrections, or restatements to previously reported revenue figures. Also include discussions of revenue performance relative to budget or prior periods, revenue growth assumptions used in financial models, and any communications questioning or challenging revenue figures reported by MedCore management.
127	
128	**Key Custodian Focus:** Diana Cheng-Rourke, as a member of MedCore\'s board of directors, would have received regular financial reporting including revenue data. Tobias Krell, as the deal execution lead, was involved in financial monitoring and reporting. Dr. Priya Anand, as CEO, was the primary source of revenue information from MedCore management. Garrett Whitford, as Managing Partner, would have been included on significant revenue-related communications.
129	
130	**MedCore Revenue Figures for Reference:** Reviewers should be aware of MedCore\'s reported revenue during the relevant period for context:
131	
132	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
133	  **Fiscal Year**                     **Reported Revenue**
134	  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
135	  FY2019                              \$78 million
136	
137	  FY2020                              \$96 million
138	
139	  FY2021                              \$118 million
140	
141	  FY2022                              \$142 million
142	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
143	
144	**Multi-Category Tagging:** Documents that discuss revenue in the context of the Confidential Information Memorandum, the sale process, or MedCore valuations should be tagged to Category 2 and also to Category 4 (CIM and Marketing Materials), Category 12 (Stock Purchase Agreement), or Category 18 (Valuation Documents), as applicable.
145	
146	**[III.C. Request Category 3 --- FDA 510(k) Materials]{.underline}**
147	
148	**Responsive:** All documents relating to MedCore Diagnostics Inc.\'s FDA 510(k) premarket notification clearance applications, including internal assessments of regulatory readiness, correspondence with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, consultant and regulatory counsel reports, testing and validation data, and any analysis of the likelihood or expected timeline of clearance.
149	
150	**Known Pending Applications.** At the time of the sale to Veriton Health Systems Inc., MedCore had two 510(k) applications pending with the FDA:
151	
152	> • **MC-510k-2021-04**, submitted in June 2021, for the \"VeriScan Pro\" rapid testing platform, a point-of-care diagnostic device designed for rapid analyte detection in clinical laboratory and hospital settings.
153	>
154	> • **MC-510k-2022-01**, submitted in February 2022, for the \"CoreAssay Plus\" multiplex panel, a multi-analyte immunoassay panel intended for use with MedCore\'s installed base of diagnostic analyzers.
155	
156	**Specific Document Types to Include:** All drafts of 510(k) submissions, pre-submission meeting requests and minutes, FDA correspondence (including deficiency letters, requests for additional information, and any FDA determination letters), internal emails and memoranda discussing FDA submission status or strategy, reports and communications from regulatory consultants, validation testing protocols and results, clinical data analyses, and any internal assessments discussing the probability, timeline, or risks associated with obtaining 510(k) clearance.
157	
158	**Note --- High Priority Category:** This is a high-priority category given the government\'s apparent focus on alleged misrepresentations regarding MedCore\'s FDA regulatory status during the sale process. Reviewers should apply a broad interpretation of \"relating to\" for this category. Documents that touch upon MedCore\'s regulatory posture, product approval status, or FDA interactions should be tagged to Category 3 even if the reference is brief or incidental to the document\'s primary subject matter.
159	
160	**Multi-Category Tagging:** Reviewers should consider whether FDA-related documents are additionally responsive to Category 4 (if FDA status was discussed in or reflected in CIM materials), Category 7 (if FDA status was discussed at board meetings), or Category 9 (if concerns or complaints about regulatory compliance or the accuracy of regulatory representations are present). Tag all applicable categories.
161	
162	Communications with regulatory counsel regarding FDA matters are responsive to Category 3 but must also be reviewed for privilege in accordance with the instructions in Section V.
163	
164	**[III.D. Request Category 4 --- CIM and Marketing Materials]{.underline}**
165	
166	**Responsive:** All documents relating to the preparation, review, revision, approval, or distribution of any Confidential Information Memorandum (\"CIM\"), investor presentations, teasers, management presentations, or other marketing materials created in connection with the sale of MedCore Diagnostics Inc. to prospective buyers.
167	
168	**Specific Document Types to Include:** All drafts of the CIM (including versions with tracked changes, comments, or margin annotations), final versions distributed to prospective buyers, distribution lists reflecting which parties received the CIM, data room indexes and data room contents, management presentation slides and scripts, teaser documents or \"blind profiles\" distributed before NDA execution, any Q&A documents or supplemental materials provided to potential buyers, and all internal communications discussing the content, accuracy, completeness, or revisions of the CIM or other marketing materials.
169	
170	**Key Custodians:** Tobias Krell managed the CIM preparation process and oversaw the virtual data room. Diana Cheng-Rourke and Garrett Whitford were involved in reviewing and approving the CIM content. Dr. Priya Anand, as CEO, provided management input and participated in management presentations.
171	
172	**Investment Banker Overlap: Communications with Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co. regarding the content or drafting of the CIM should be tagged to both Category 4 and Category 6 (Investment Banker / Financial Advisor Communications).**
173	
174	**Note --- Critical Category:** The CIM is a central document in the government\'s investigation. Any document reflecting discussions about what information to include in or exclude from the CIM, discussions about the accuracy or completeness of representations made in the CIM, or discussions about revisions to the CIM following internal or external feedback should be coded responsive to this category and flagged for escalation to Jordan Tavares. This is especially true for documents in which the accuracy of specific CIM content is questioned, debated, or revised.
175	
176	**Particular Attention Areas.** Reviewers should pay particular attention to CIM content and related internal discussions regarding the following topics, which are of heightened relevance to the government\'s investigation:
177	
178	> \(a\) MedCore\'s historical revenue figures and forward-looking revenue growth projections, including the assumptions underlying such projections;
179	>
180	> \(b\) The status of FDA 510(k) applications and anticipated clearance timelines, including any representations about the likelihood of approval for the VeriScan Pro or CoreAssay Plus products; and
181	>
182	> \(c\) VeriScan Pro testing accuracy data, including sensitivity and specificity metrics cited in the CIM or management presentations and the underlying validation studies supporting such metrics.
183	
184	Documents addressing any of these three topics in connection with the CIM or sale marketing materials should be treated as high-priority responsive documents and escalated for secondary review.
185	
186	**[III.E. Request Category 5 --- Buyer Communications]{.underline}**
187	
188	**Responsive:** All communications between Ridgeline partners or employees and any potential buyer or buyer\'s representative regarding the sale of MedCore Diagnostics Inc.
189	
190	This category encompasses all communications with Veriton Health Systems Inc. (the ultimate buyer) and its advisors, as well as any other parties who received the CIM, executed non-disclosure agreements, or otherwise participated in the sale process, regardless of whether such parties ultimately submitted indications of interest or proceeded to definitive documentation.
191	
192	**Specific Document Types to Include:** Initial outreach and market-sounding communications, NDA transmittals and executed NDAs, indications of interest and letters of intent, follow-up diligence questions and responses, management presentation scheduling and logistics, negotiation communications regarding price, structure, and deal terms, post-signing and pre-closing communications (including closing conditions satisfaction), and any post-closing communications regarding the transaction.
193	
194	**Time Frame Focus:** The primary time period for this category is approximately mid-2022 through November 18, 2022 (the sale closing date), corresponding to the active sale process. However, earlier market-sounding communications and preliminary buyer interactions are also responsive. Post-closing communications relating to purchase price adjustments, indemnification, or representations and warranties are responsive and should also be tagged to Category 13.
195	
196	**[III.F. Request Category 6 --- Investment Banker / Financial Advisor Communications]{.underline}**
197	
198	**Responsive:** All communications between Ridgeline partners or employees and any investment banker, broker, or financial advisor regarding the sale of MedCore Diagnostics Inc.
199	
200	**Primary Entity: Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co., which was engaged as the exclusive financial advisor to Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC in connection with the sale of MedCore. All communications with Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn personnel are presumptively responsive to this category if they relate to MedCore or the sale process.**
201	
202	**Specific Document Types to Include:** The engagement letter and any amendments thereto, fee arrangements and success fee calculations, all substantive communications regarding sale process strategy, buyer outreach and market feedback, valuation analyses and pricing recommendations, deal structure advice, process timeline management, and any communications regarding the content of marketing materials (which should also be tagged to Category 4).
203	
204	**Note Regarding Garrett Whitford. Garrett Whitford is a former employee of Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn & Co. and maintains personal relationships with several current Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn personnel. Communications between Whitford and Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn personnel should be tagged responsive to Category 6 if they relate in any way to MedCore, the MedCore sale process, or Ridgeline fund business, regardless of whether the communication is characterized as \"personal,\" \"social,\" or \"catching up.\" The relevant question is whether the substance of the communication touches upon MedCore or the sale, not the characterization of the relationship. Communications between Whitford and Cromdale Consulting Aldwyn personnel that are purely social in nature with no reference whatsoever to MedCore, the sale, or fund business may be coded non-responsive, but reviewers should err on the side of coding as responsive when the communication contains even a passing reference to business matters.**
205	
206	If any other financial advisors, brokers, or intermediaries were involved in the sale process or provided valuation-related services in connection with MedCore, communications with such parties should also be captured under this category.
207	
208	**[III.G. Request Category 7 --- MedCore Board Materials]{.underline}**
209	
210	**Responsive:** All board of directors meeting minutes, resolutions, written consents, unanimous written consents, and board packages (including all attachments, exhibits, and supplemental materials) for MedCore Diagnostics Inc. from April 2020 (the first board meeting following the acquisition closing) through November 2022 (the sale closing).
211	
212	Board packages typically include financial statements, management reports and operating updates, regulatory status updates, strategic planning materials, committee reports (audit committee, compensation committee), and materials submitted for board approval. All such materials are responsive when included as part of a board package or referenced in board minutes.
213	
214	**Key Custodian:** Diana Cheng-Rourke served on MedCore\'s board of directors throughout Ridgeline\'s ownership period; her files are expected to be a primary source of board materials. Dr. Priya Anand, as CEO, prepared or oversaw the preparation of management reports and presentations to the board.
215	
216	**Multi-Category Tagging:** Board materials should be tagged to all additional categories implicated by their content. If board minutes discuss revenue performance, tag to Category 2. If they discuss FDA 510(k) status, tag to Category 3. If they include financial statements, tag to Category 8. If they discuss MedCore\'s valuation or strategic value, tag to Category 18. If they discuss management compensation or equity plans, tag to Category 14.
217	
218	**[III.H. Request Category 8 --- Financial Statements and Audit Reports]{.underline}**
219	
220	**Responsive:** All documents relating to MedCore Diagnostics Inc.\'s financial statements (annual, quarterly, and monthly), audit reports, audit management letters, and any adjustments, corrections, or restatements to financial statements during the relevant period.

76	
77	The work product doctrine protects from disclosure documents and tangible things prepared in anticipation of litigation or for trial by or for a party or its representative. **UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION** **DIVISION OF ENFORCEMENT**

100 Pearl Street, Suite 20-100 New York, New York 10004 Telephone: (212) 555-0100 Facsimile: (212) 555-0101

October 28, 2024

**VIA FEDERAL EXPRESS AND EMAIL**

Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC

Attn: Priya Venkatesh, Co-Founder & Chief Operating Officer

425 Park Avenue, 31st Floor New York, New York 10022

**Re: Document Preservation Notice --- In the Matter of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC (Investigation File No. NY-2024-0871)**

Dear Ms. Venkatesh:

The Division of Enforcement (the \"Staff\") of the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"Commission\") is conducting a non-public, fact-finding investigation into Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC (\"Ridgeline\" or the \"Firm\") concerning potential violations of the federal securities laws, including but not limited to Section 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder. This letter constitutes formal notice of Ridgeline\'s obligation to preserve all documents and electronically stored information (\"ESI\") that may be relevant to the investigation described herein. The obligation to preserve documents and ESI attaches immediately upon receipt of this letter. You must take all necessary steps to ensure that potentially relevant materials are identified, secured, and preserved in their current form without alteration, destruction, or deletion of any kind.

**Scope of Investigation. The investigation concerns the valuation of portfolio companies held by Ridgeline Capital Partners Fund III LP (\"Fund III\"), and the use of such valuations in fundraising materials, investor communications, and marketing presentations distributed to current and prospective limited partners during the period from January 1, 2020 through the present (the \"Relevant Period\"). The investigation specifically concerns, among other things, valuations reported for portfolio companies including but not limited to Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc. and Meridian Industrial Solutions LLC, fundraising activities for Fund III including the fundraising push culminating in the final close, and communications with investors, auditors, and third-party valuation firms in connection with any of the foregoing.**

**Categories of Documents to Be Preserved.** Ridgeline must preserve the following categories of documents and ESI, without limitation, to the extent they relate to Fund III or the subject matter described above during the Relevant Period:

> *(a) Valuation-Related Documents.* All documents relating to the valuation of any Fund III portfolio company, including but not limited to: valuation models, discounted cash flow analyses, comparable company analyses, investment committee memoranda, board materials, internal memoranda, and any drafts or working papers relating thereto. All communications with Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC or any other third-party valuation firm regarding Fund III portfolio company valuations. All communications with Northvale Accounting Group LLP or any other accounting firm relating to Fund III portfolio company valuations or fund-level financial statements.
>
> *(b) Fundraising and Investor Communications.* All documents relating to the formation, marketing, and fundraising of Fund III, including private placement memoranda, limited partnership agreements, subscription agreements, investor presentations, pitch books, due diligence questionnaire responses, and side letters. All communications with current or prospective limited partners, placement agents, or investors concerning Fund III performance, returns, portfolio company valuations, or the status of Fund III fundraising.
>
> *(c) Internal Policies and Compliance.* All valuation policies, procedures, guidelines, and compliance manuals in effect at any time during the Relevant Period. All documents relating to any internal review, audit, or compliance inquiry concerning Ridgeline\'s valuation practices or methodologies.
>
> *(d) Personnel Communications.* All communications --- including emails, text messages, instant messages, voicemails, and any other form of electronic communication --- among Ridgeline officers, directors, employees, and agents relating to Fund III portfolio company valuations, fundraising, or any other matter within the scope of this investigation. This includes, without limitation, communications stored on personal devices, including mobile phones, personal email accounts, and messaging applications such as iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal, and any similar platforms.
>
> *(e) Compensation and Performance Records.* All documents relating to the compensation, bonuses, carried interest allocations, management fee calculations, or other remuneration of any Ridgeline principal or employee, to the extent such compensation is tied to or calculated based on fund performance, assets under management, or portfolio company valuations.
>
> *(f) Acquisition and Due Diligence Materials.* All documents relating to the acquisition of any Fund III portfolio company, including due diligence reports, financial projections, term sheets, letters of intent, purchase agreements, and closing documents.

**Preservation Instructions.** In addition to preserving the categories of documents enumerated above, Ridgeline must comply with the following specific directives:

> 1\. *Immediate Suspension of Document Destruction.* Ridgeline must immediately suspend any routine document retention or destruction policies, auto-delete functions, or recycling schedules that could result in the destruction, overwriting, or loss of potentially relevant documents or ESI.
>
> 2\. *Electronic Data.* Ridgeline must preserve all ESI in its native format, including all associated metadata. You must not alter, delete, overwrite, or otherwise modify any electronic files, emails, databases, or backup tapes. This preservation obligation extends to data stored on servers, desktop computers, laptop computers, mobile devices (including personal cell phones), tablets, cloud storage accounts (including but not limited to iCloud, Google Drive, and Dropbox), and any CRM, portfolio management, or other business software platforms used by the Firm or its personnel.
>
> 3\. *Custodian Notification.* Ridgeline must promptly notify all current and former officers, directors, employees, and agents who may possess relevant documents or ESI of this preservation obligation. Ridgeline should implement a litigation hold and distribute written hold notices to all such individuals without delay.
>
> 4\. *Third-Party Custodians.* To the extent relevant documents are in the possession, custody, or control of third parties --- including but not limited to outside accountants, valuation consultants, fund administrators, and legal counsel --- Ridgeline must take reasonable steps to ensure the preservation of such documents.
>
> 5\. *Backup and Archival Systems.* Ridgeline must preserve all backup tapes, disaster recovery tapes, and archival media that may contain relevant documents or ESI.

**Consequences of Non-Compliance.** The Commission takes document preservation obligations with the utmost seriousness. Failure to preserve relevant documents and ESI may result in an enforcement action for obstruction or spoliation of evidence, adverse inference instructions in any subsequent administrative or judicial proceeding, and referral to the United States Department of Justice for potential criminal prosecution for obstruction of justice under 18 U.S.C. § 1519 or other applicable federal statutes. Any destruction, alteration, or concealment of potentially relevant documents after receipt of this letter may constitute a separate and independent violation of federal law, regardless of the ultimate disposition of the underlying investigation.

**Contact and Acknowledgment.** Please direct any questions regarding the scope of this preservation obligation to the undersigned, Harrison Caldwell, Senior Staff Attorney, Division of Enforcement, at (212) 555-0193 or h.caldwell@sec-fictional.gov. The Staff requests that Ridgeline provide written confirmation of receipt of this letter and confirmation that a litigation hold has been implemented within ten (10) business days of receipt of this letter. In addition, please identify a designated point of contact at Ridgeline for purposes of the investigation.

This letter does not constitute a formal order of investigation, nor does it mean that the Commission or its staff has concluded that any person or entity has violated any provision of the federal securities laws. The investigation is non-public, and the Commission requests that you treat this matter, including the existence of the investigation, confidentially.

Very truly yours,

UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION DIVISION OF ENFORCEMENT

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Harrison Caldwell Senior Staff Attorney Division of Enforcement U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission 100 Pearl Street, Suite 20-100 New York, New York 10004 Telephone: (212) 555-0193

**[Portfolio Company Review --- Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc.]{.underline}**

**Company Overview. Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc. is a Delaware corporation and clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel oncology therapeutics. Aldersgate\'s proprietary platform targets specific tumor microenvironment pathways and has yielded a pipeline of candidates in various stages of preclinical and clinical development. The transaction was led by Jonathan Kessler, Director of Investments at Ridgeline Capital Partners. The investment represents a control position in Aldersgate and includes representation on the company\'s board of directors.**

**Valuation as of December 31, 2023. The investment in Aldersgate Therapeutics was carried at a fair value of approximately \$285 million as of December 31, 2023, reflecting updated comparable company and discounted cash flow analyses performed during the fourth quarter of 2023. The quarterly valuation opinion supporting this carrying value was provided by Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC in accordance with the firm\'s standard engagement procedures. The year-end carrying value reflects the application of both market-based and income-based approaches, weighted according to the relative reliability and relevance of each methodology in light of the company\'s stage of development and available market data.**

**Operational Update. During 2023, Aldersgate continued to advance its lead therapeutic candidates through clinical development, achieving several important milestones. The company completed enrollment in a pivotal Phase 2 clinical trial for its most advanced compound and reported encouraging interim efficacy and safety data. Aldersgate also expanded its clinical operations team and strengthened its intellectual property portfolio through the filing of additional patent applications covering its proprietary platform technology. **Company Overview.** Meridian Industrial Solutions LLC is an Ohio limited liability company specializing in industrial automation systems, process optimization, and advanced manufacturing solutions. **Valuation History and Q1 2023 Valuation Adjustment.** As of the prior reporting period (Q4 2022), Meridian was carried at a fair value of \$152 million, reflecting strong growth in revenue and order backlog during the first year of Ridgeline\'s ownership. The revised valuation was supported by an updated analysis prepared by Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC, which applied refreshed inputs to both the comparable company and discounted cash flow methodologies. The Fund\'s investment committee reviewed the revised carrying value in its March 2023 revaluation discussion and approved the downward adjustment as appropriate under the circumstances and consistent with the firm\'s Valuation Policy and Procedures Manual.

**Valuation as of December 31, 2023.** Following the Q1 2023 adjustment, Meridian\'s operating performance improved over the balance of the year as the company secured several significant new automation contracts with major automotive and aerospace manufacturers and benefited from a gradual recovery in order activity. **[Valuation Methodology and Governance]{.underline}**

Ridgeline Capital Partners is committed to rigorous, independent, and transparent valuation practices for all portfolio investments. All fair value determinations for Fund III portfolio companies are made in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820 --- Fair Value Measurement (\"ASC 820\") and the firm\'s Valuation Policy and Procedures Manual, which was last updated in February 2023. The manual sets forth the governing framework for the frequency, methodology, and approval process applicable to all fair value determinations across the firm\'s fund complex.

Quarterly valuations of each portfolio company are performed with input from Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC, an independent third-party valuation firm. Pinehurst provides valuation opinions based on one or more of the following methodologies, as appropriate given the nature and stage of each investment: (i) comparable company analysis, (ii) precedent transaction analysis, and (iii) discounted cash flow analysis. The selection and weighting of methodologies are determined based on the availability and reliability of relevant market data, the specific characteristics of the portfolio company, and prevailing market conditions.

All quarterly valuations are reviewed and approved by the Fund\'s investment committee, which is chaired by Marcus Delacroix, Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer. The investment committee\'s review process includes consideration of the independent valuation opinions provided by Pinehurst, the recommendations of the deal team responsible for each portfolio company, and any other information deemed relevant to the fair value determination.

Adjustments to carrying values are made when warranted by changes in market conditions, company operating performance, comparable company data, or other relevant factors. **RIDGELINE CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC**

**COMPLIANCE MANUAL**

**SECTION 7: VALUATION POLICIES AND PROCEDURES**

**(EXCERPT)**

**Effective Date of Current Manual Version:** February 2023 **Prior Version Date:** June 2020 **Original Adoption Date:** March 2014

**Prepared by:** Neil Banerjee, Compliance Officer, in coordination with Priya Venkatesh, Co-founder & COO

**Approved by:** Marcus Delacroix, Co-founder, Managing Partner & CIO

**Entity:** Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company formed in 2014, with principal offices located at 425 Park Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022

CONFIDENTIAL --- This document is intended solely for internal use by authorized personnel of Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC and its affiliated entities. Unauthorized reproduction, distribution, or disclosure of any portion of this document is strictly prohibited.

**[Section 7: Valuation Policies and Procedures --- Overview]{.underline}**

This Section 7 of the Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC (\"Ridgeline\" or the \"Firm\") Compliance Manual (this \"Manual\") establishes the Firm\'s policies and procedures governing the valuation of portfolio company investments held across all investment funds managed by Ridgeline. These policies apply to Ridgeline Capital Partners Fund III LP, a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2021 (together with its parallel vehicles, \"Fund III\"), as well as all predecessor funds managed by the Firm, including Ridgeline Capital Partners Fund I LP (approximately \$380 million in committed capital, \"Fund I\") and Ridgeline Capital Partners Fund II LP (approximately \$620 million in committed capital, \"Fund II,\" and together with Fund I and Fund III, the \"Funds\").

Ridgeline\'s valuation framework is designed to ensure that the Firm\'s fair value determinations comply with all applicable regulatory requirements, including the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820, *Fair Value Measurement* (\"ASC 820\"), and applicable guidance issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (\"SEC\") for registered investment advisers. The Firm is committed to maintaining a robust, transparent, and internally consistent approach to valuation that serves the interests of the Firm\'s limited partners and satisfies the Firm\'s fiduciary obligations.

The detailed valuation procedures that implement the policies described in this Section 7 are contained in a separate, standalone document entitled the \"Valuation Policy and Procedures Manual\" (the \"Valuation Manual\"). The Valuation Policy and Procedures Manual (current version: February 2023; prior version: June 2020) is incorporated herein by reference and should be read in conjunction with this Section 7. All Ridgeline personnel involved in the valuation process are expected to be familiar with both this Section 7 and the Valuation Manual.

The Valuation Manual is jointly maintained by the Compliance Officer, Neil Banerjee, and the Chief Financial Officer, Samantha Pryce, with final approval authority resting with the Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer, Marcus Delacroix, and the Chief Operating Officer, Priya Venkatesh. Any questions regarding the interpretation or application of this Section 7 or the Valuation Manual should be directed to Mr. Banerjee.

**[Section 7.1: Valuation Manual --- Scope and Version History]{.underline}**

**7.1.1 Scope.** The Valuation Manual applies to all portfolio company investments held by any Ridgeline-managed fund, regardless of investment stage, sector, geographic location, or instrument type. This includes equity investments, debt instruments, co-investment vehicles, and any other financial interests in portfolio companies. The Valuation Manual governs both the initial valuation of newly acquired investments and the ongoing periodic revaluation of such investments throughout the holding period and through final realization.

**7.1.2 Version History**

The Valuation Manual has been revised from time to time to reflect changes in applicable accounting standards, regulatory guidance, and the Firm\'s evolving investment portfolio. The following is the complete version history of the Valuation Manual:

  **Version**             **Effective Date**   **Summary of Key Changes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   **Approving Parties**
  ----------------------- -------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------

Covered valuation methodologies applicable to Ridgeline Capital Partners Fund I LP.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Marcus Delacroix; Priya Venkatesh

  Version 2.0             June 2020            Revised to incorporate updated ASC 820 guidance and expanded methodology sections applicable to Fund II portfolio companies. Added enhanced documentation requirements for comparable company selection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Marcus Delacroix; Priya Venkatesh

  Version 3.0 (Current)   February 2023        Revised to reflect additional valuation methodologies for Fund III portfolio companies, including sector-specific approaches for life sciences companies (relevant to Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc., a Delaware corporation, acquired September 17, 2021 for approximately \$145 million) and industrial/manufacturing companies (relevant to Meridian Industrial Solutions LLC, an Ohio limited liability company, acquired March 8, 2022 for approximately \$88 million).   Marcus Delacroix; Priya Venkatesh
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All prior versions of the Valuation Manual shall be retained in accordance with Section 7.5 (Record Retention) below.

Key changes from Version 2.0 (June 2020) to Version 3.0 (February 2023) included the following:

> \(a\) Addition of revenue-based and pipeline-based valuation approaches for life sciences portfolio companies, reflecting the unique characteristics of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies with pre-revenue or early-revenue-stage profiles;
>
> \(b\) Updated comparable company selection criteria, including enhanced screening parameters and documentation requirements for public market comparable identification;
>
> \(c\) Revised escalation procedures for valuation disputes, including clarification of the process by which dissenting views within the Valuation Committee are resolved and documented; and
>
> \(d\) Alignment with third-party valuation advisor engagement procedures, including updated protocols for the engagement and oversight of Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC, a New York limited liability company (\"Pinehurst\"), the Firm\'s primary independent valuation advisor.

**[Section 7.2: Valuation Committee --- Composition and Meeting Requirements]{.underline}**

**7.2.1 Composition.** Ridgeline maintains a Valuation Committee (the \"Valuation Committee\") responsible for the oversight, review, and approval of all portfolio company valuations across the Funds. The Valuation Committee is composed of the following standing members:

> **Chair:** Marcus Delacroix, Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer
>
> **Standing Members:**
>
> • Priya Venkatesh, Co-founder & Chief Operating Officer
>
> • Samantha Pryce, Chief Financial Officer
>
> • Neil Banerjee, Compliance Officer
>
> • The designated deal lead for each portfolio company under review (e.g., Jonathan Kessler, Director of Investments, for Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc.; Ava Chen, Vice President, for Meridian Industrial Solutions LLC)

The Valuation Committee may also include other members of the Firm\'s investment committee as appropriate, including but not limited to T. Nakamura and D. Fitzgerald, who serve as investment committee participants and attend Valuation Committee meetings on a rotating basis depending on the portfolio companies under review. The Chair may invite additional attendees with relevant expertise to participate in Valuation Committee meetings on an advisory, non-voting basis.

**7.2.2 Meeting Frequency**

The Valuation Committee shall convene no less frequently than once per calendar quarter to review and approve the fair value determinations for all portfolio company investments. Additional meetings may be called by the Chair or by any two standing members of the Valuation Committee in the event of a material development affecting the valuation of one or more portfolio companies, including but not limited to a significant change in financial performance, a triggering event under the terms of a portfolio company\'s credit agreements, or a regulatory development with material valuation implications. Meeting dates shall be scheduled by the Compliance Officer in advance of each calendar quarter to the extent practicable.

**7.2.3 Meeting Minutes**

Minutes of each Valuation Committee meeting shall be prepared by the Compliance Officer or his or her designee and maintained in accordance with Section 7.5 (Record Retention) below. Meeting minutes shall include, at a minimum, the date of the meeting, the names of all attendees, a summary of each portfolio company valuation reviewed, the methodologies applied, the recommended and approved fair values, and a record of any dissenting views expressed by Valuation Committee members.

**7.2.4 Responsibilities.** The Valuation Committee\'s responsibilities include the following:

> \(a\) Reviewing valuation recommendations prepared by deal leads for each portfolio company investment;
>
> \(b\) Considering third-party valuation reports prepared by Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC (key contact: Sandra Yeung, Managing Director) and other independent advisors as applicable;
>
> \(c\) Reviewing and approving quarterly Net Asset Value (\"NAV\") calculations for each Fund;
>
> \(d\) Reviewing and approving valuation adjustments, including any restatements or revisions to previously reported fair values;
>
> \(e\) Ensuring consistency of all valuation determinations with the policies and methodologies set forth in the Valuation Manual; and
>
> \(f\) Documenting the rationale for all material valuation judgments, including the basis for selecting particular methodologies and key assumptions.

Valuation Committee decisions shall be reached by majority vote of the standing members present, provided that a quorum of at least three standing members (including the Chair or the Chair\'s designee) is present. Any dissenting views shall be recorded in the meeting minutes, together with a summary of the basis for the dissenting member\'s position.

**[Section 7.3: Third-Party Valuation Advisors]{.underline}**

Ridgeline recognizes the importance of independent third-party valuation analysis in supporting the integrity and credibility of the Firm\'s fair value determinations. It is the Firm\'s policy to engage independent third-party valuation firms to provide advisory opinions and analyses in connection with the valuation of portfolio company investments.

Ridgeline engages **Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC**, a New York limited liability company (\"Pinehurst\"), as its primary third-party valuation advisor. Pinehurst provides fairness opinions, quarterly portfolio company valuation analyses, and ad hoc advisory services as requested by the Firm. The Firm\'s primary contact at Pinehurst is Sandra Yeung, Managing Director. The engagement of Pinehurst is governed by engagement letters executed for each annual or project-specific engagement. Engagement letters shall be reviewed and approved by the CFO (Samantha Pryce) and the Compliance Officer (Neil Banerjee) prior to execution.

The engagement process operates as follows: Pinehurst prepares and delivers draft valuation reports to the designated deal lead and the CFO for initial review and comment. Following any necessary revisions and discussions between Pinehurst and the deal team, final reports are presented to the Valuation Committee for consideration in connection with the Committee\'s quarterly valuation review. All communications with Pinehurst, including engagement letters, draft and final valuation reports, data requests, methodology discussion memoranda, and related correspondence, shall be maintained in the Firm\'s document management system and retained in accordance with Section 7.5 (Record Retention) below.

In addition to Pinehurst, the Firm engages **Northvale Accounting Group LLP**, a Connecticut limited liability partnership (\"Northvale\"), as its independent auditor. Northvale performs annual audits of each Fund\'s financial statements and, in connection therewith, reviews portfolio company valuations as part of its audit procedures. All communications with Northvale regarding portfolio company valuations, including audit inquiry letters, work papers provided to Northvale, and audit findings relating to valuation matters, shall likewise be retained in accordance with Section 7.5.

Deal leads are expected to serve as the primary points of contact with Pinehurst for company-specific valuation matters. For example, Jonathan Kessler, Director of Investments, serves as the primary contact for all Pinehurst engagements relating to Aldersgate Therapeutics Inc., and Ava Chen, Vice President, serves as the primary contact for Meridian Industrial Solutions LLC. The CFO, Samantha Pryce, coordinates firm-wide valuation reporting, including the aggregation of individual portfolio company valuations into fund-level NAV calculations and the preparation of consolidated valuation summaries for the Valuation Committee.

**[Section 7.4: Valuation Methodologies --- Summary Reference]{.underline}**

This Section 7.4 provides a high-level summary of the approved valuation methodologies referenced in the Valuation Manual. This section is intended as a cross-reference guide only; the full description, implementation guidance, and assumptions documentation requirements for each methodology are set forth in the Valuation Manual itself, to which all investment professionals and other relevant personnel should refer.

The following valuation methodologies have been approved for use by the Firm in determining the fair value of portfolio company investments:

> \(a\) **Discounted Cash Flow (\"DCF\") Analysis:** A forward-looking methodology based on the present value of projected future cash flows, using an appropriate discount rate reflective of the risk profile of the investment.
>
> \(b\) **Comparable Company Analysis (Public Market Multiples):** A market-based approach that derives implied valuations from the trading multiples of publicly listed companies with comparable financial, operational, and sector characteristics.
>
> \(c\) **Comparable Transaction Analysis (Precedent Transactions):** A market-based approach that derives implied valuations from the transaction multiples observed in completed acquisitions of companies with comparable characteristics.
>
> \(d\) **Option Pricing Model (\"OPM\"):** A model-based approach used to allocate enterprise value across complex capital structures with multiple classes of equity or equity-linked instruments, including preferred equity, convertible instruments, and management incentive arrangements.
>
> \(e\) **Adjusted Net Asset Value:** An asset-based approach in which the fair values of individual assets and liabilities are estimated and aggregated to determine the net value of the enterprise.
>
> \(f\) **Revenue-Based and Pipeline-Based Approaches for Life Sciences Companies:** Sector-specific methodologies added in the February 2023 update to the Valuation Manual, designed for application to portfolio companies with pre-revenue or early-revenue-stage profiles, including but not limited to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies with product candidates in clinical development.

The Valuation Manual specifies the circumstances under which each methodology is appropriate, the key assumptions that must be documented in connection with the application of each methodology, and the procedures for selecting primary and secondary (corroborative) approaches. The selection of valuation methodologies for any particular portfolio company is subject to review and approval by the Valuation Committee.

The Firm\'s investor relations team, led by Robert Galindo, Director of Investor Relations, is responsible for incorporating Valuation Committee-approved valuations into investor communications, quarterly reports, annual reports, and fundraising materials. Mr. Galindo and his team must ensure that all valuation figures used in external materials correspond to the fair values approved by the Valuation Committee, and that no preliminary, unapproved, or superseded valuation figures are disseminated to investors or prospective investors.

**[Section 7.5: Record Retention Requirements]{.underline}**

This Section 7.5 establishes the Firm\'s record retention requirements for valuation-related documents. Compliance with these retention requirements is mandatory and is subject to monitoring and enforcement by the Compliance Officer in accordance with Section 7.6 (Compliance Monitoring and Internal Review) below.

The following categories of documents shall be retained for the minimum periods specified:

> \(a\) **Valuation Manual Versions.** All versions of the Valuation Policy and Procedures Manual, including superseded versions, shall be retained for a minimum of **seven (7) years** following the date on which such version was superseded. For the avoidance of doubt, the June 2020 version of the Valuation Manual (Version 2.0), which was superseded by the current February 2023 version (Version 3.0), must be retained until at least February 2030. Version 1.0 (March 2014), which was superseded in June 2020, must be retained until at least June 2027.
>
> \(b\) **Valuation Committee Meeting Minutes.** Minutes of all Valuation Committee meetings shall be retained for a minimum of **seven (7) years** from the date of the meeting. Given the Valuation Committee\'s obligation to meet no less frequently than once per calendar quarter (as set forth in Section 7.2.2 above), meeting minutes shall be maintained for each quarterly meeting.
>
> \(c\) **Third-Party Valuation Reports and Related Correspondence.** All third-party valuation reports, engagement letters, and related correspondence (including communications with Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC and Northvale Accounting Group LLP) shall be retained for a minimum of **seven (7) years** from the date of such report or communication.
>
> \(d\) **Valuation Models and Supporting Analyses.** All valuation models, supporting analyses, comparable company analyses, discounted cash flow models, and related working papers prepared in connection with portfolio company valuations shall be retained for a minimum of **seven (7) years** from the date of the applicable valuation determination.
>
> \(e\) **Investor Communications Referencing Valuations.** All investor communications, quarterly reports, annual reports, capital account statements, and other materials that reference portfolio company valuations or fund performance shall be retained for a minimum of **seven (7) years** from the date of distribution.

Records shall be maintained in Ridgeline\'s document management system and/or on the Firm\'s shared network drives, in a manner that permits efficient retrieval and production. The Compliance Officer, Neil Banerjee, is responsible for ensuring the Firm\'s compliance with the retention obligations set forth in this Section 7.5, including periodic verification that records are being properly maintained and that no documents have been improperly destroyed or deleted.

The destruction of any records subject to a legal hold, regulatory investigation, or preservation notice is **strictly prohibited**, regardless of whether the applicable retention period has expired. Any document preservation directives issued by legal counsel or regulatory authorities supersede the standard retention schedules set forth herein. All Ridgeline personnel are required to comply with any such directives immediately upon receipt and to direct any questions regarding the scope of a preservation directive to the Compliance Officer or outside counsel.

**[Section 7.6: Compliance Monitoring and Internal Review]{.underline}**

Neil Banerjee, as Compliance Officer, is responsible for conducting an annual review of the Firm\'s valuation practices and procedures to ensure adherence to the Valuation Manual and this Section 7. The annual review shall be completed no later than the end of the first quarter of each calendar year, covering the valuation activity of the preceding calendar year.

Any concerns, discrepancies, or potential violations identified during such reviews shall be reported promptly to the COO, Priya Venkatesh, and, if warranted based on the nature or severity of the identified issue, to outside counsel. The Compliance Officer shall exercise reasonable judgment in determining the appropriate level of escalation for any identified concern.

Findings from compliance reviews and any resulting corrective actions shall be documented in a written memorandum and retained in accordance with Section 7.5 (Record Retention) above.

The compliance review process includes, at a minimum, the following components:

> \(a\) Sampling of quarterly valuation determinations to verify consistency with the methodologies and procedures set forth in the Valuation Manual;
>
> \(b\) Verification that Valuation Committee meetings were held at the required quarterly frequency and that meeting minutes were prepared, documented, and retained;
>
> \(c\) Review of third-party valuation advisor engagement compliance, including confirmation that engagement letters were properly executed and that Pinehurst Valuation Advisors LLC reports were obtained and considered by the Valuation Committee; and
>
> \(d\) Spot-checking of investor materials, including quarterly reports and capital account statements, against Valuation Committee-approved valuations to confirm accuracy and consistency.

**[Section 7.7: Amendments and Updates]{.underline}**

Any amendments to this Section 7 of the Compliance Manual or to the Valuation Manual must be approved by the Managing Partner & CIO, Marcus Delacroix, and the COO, Priya Venkatesh, with input from the Compliance Officer, Neil Banerjee, and the CFO, Samantha Pryce. No amendment shall be effective until it has received the written approval of both Mr. Delacroix and Ms. Venkatesh.

All amendments shall be documented with an effective date and version number, and prior versions of the amended document shall be archived in accordance with the record retention policy set forth in Section 7.5 above. A summary description of the material changes effected by each amendment shall be prepared and circulated to all relevant Ridgeline personnel.

The most recent amendment to the Valuation Manual was adopted in February 2023 (Version 3.0). As of the current date, no further amendments to the Valuation Manual have been adopted or are pending approval.

*End of Section 7*

Unauthorized distribution, reproduction, or disclosure is strictly prohibited.

from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def new_doc():
    d = Document()
    st = d.styles["Normal"]
    st.font.name = "Times New Roman"; st.font.size = Pt(11)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Times New Roman")
    pf = st.paragraph_format; pf.space_after = Pt(6); pf.space_before = Pt(0)
    for lvl, sz in [(1, 13), (2, 12), (3, 11)]:
        h = d.styles["Heading %d" % lvl]
        h.font.name = "Times New Roman"; h.font.size = Pt(sz); h.font.bold = True
        h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x2A, 0x44)
        h.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Times New Roman")
        h.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(12 if lvl == 1 else 8); h.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)

    sec = d.sections[0]

    return d

def runs(p, text, size=None, color=None):
    # supports **bold** segments
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part: continue
        r = p.add_run(part)
        if i % 2 == 1: r.bold = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = color
    return p

def para(d, text, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, size=None, indent=None):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    runs(p, text, size=size)
    if bold:
        for r in p.runs: r.bold = True
    if italic:
        for r in p.runs: r.italic = True
    if align == "center": p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if indent: p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    return p

def bullet(d, text, level=0, numbered=False):
    style = "List Number" if numbered else ("List Bullet" if level == 0 else "List Bullet 2")
    p = d.add_paragraph(style=style)
    runs(p, text)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

for t in [
    "**Request 9 definition (§ III.I).** The Guide quotes Request 9 as covering “complaints, concerns, or whistleblower reports regarding MedCore’s financial reporting, revenue recognition, or regulatory compliance” and then confines it to formal-channel complaints. The Subpoena’s actual text adds “testing data integrity, product quality, clinical data accuracy,” and covers reports “whether formal or informal,” including oral reports reflected in notes. The Guide’s limitation has no basis in the Subpoena, and the Government would read it as a deliberate narrowing. The Webb email’s non-production follows directly from it, and the 10% non-responsive QC sample and the targeted QC of Whitford/Cheng-Rourke Category 9 calls (§ VIII) did not catch it. That points to a QC failure we should be ready to explain.",
    "**Request 11 default (§ III.K).** Instructing reviewers to designate ACS communications privileged “when in doubt” produced 100% withholding. Over-designation at first level is defensible only if second-level privilege QC (§ VIII) actually narrowed it. For Request 11 it did not.",
    "**Priority mismatch.** The Protocol (¶ 2.5) records that the Government designated Requests 2, 3, 4, 5 and 15 as priorities and that we would “endeavor to include a substantial volume” of them in the first production. The Guide’s Phase 1 (§ VI) prioritized Requests 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 17 and 18 and deferred 2, 3 and 15 (and 9, 11, 16) to Phase 2. The weakest categories in the production line up with that deferral. Phase 2 should be resequenced so that 3, 9, 15, 2 and 11 come first.",
    "**Internal contradictions.** The Guide says cross-custodian duplicates were not de-duplicated and that Dr. Anand’s Gmail was collected. Stratton says both statements are wrong: cross-custodian de-duplication was applied (Protocol ¶ 4.5 permits it), and the Gmail account was never collected. The Guide also dates the Protocol February 10, 2025; the letter is dated February 21, and the Tracker records execution on February 15. The Guide should be reissued as Version 2.0 with corrected facts and a corrected Request 9 definition. Reviewers should be retrained on it, and changed calls should be documented.",
]:
    bullet(d, t)

para(d, "The privilege position is the biggest single credibility risk in the production. The Subpoena (Instr. IV and the Note to Request 11) requires a log that accompanies each production and is detailed enough to assess each claim. It warns that failure to log may result in waiver. Protocol ¶ 5.3 bars deferring log entries to a later production. We are out of compliance by 2,385 documents, and the Tracker itself labels the position “NON-COMPLIANT.” (The Tracker cites “Production Protocol Letter, para. 6”; the operative provisions are ¶¶ 5.2–5.3, and ¶ 6 concerns preservation. Correct the reference before it appears in any correspondence.)")

para(d, "**Whitford device reset.** The sequence in our records is as follows. The Subpoena was served on 1/14/2025 and itself directed preservation of messaging data and disabling of auto-delete. HRK issued the hold on 1/17. The iPhone was reset (“Erase All Content and Settings,” approximately 2:47 p.m.) on 1/20. Mr. Whitford’s questionnaire of 1/24 acknowledges business use of Signal and WhatsApp. Stratton told HRK by phone on 2/4 and in writing on 2/5. The Protocol letter dated 2/21 represented that holds were in place and did not mention the reset. The Subpoena warns of 18 U.S.C. §§ 1503, 1512 and 1519 exposure. Protocol ¶ 6 obliges Counsel to disclose preservation issues affecting completeness “promptly,” and the Government will learn of the gap in any event from counterparties’ devices and from Cromdale. Our recommendations:")
